3	/// The cloud run result and its shared cleanup wording.
4	extension CloudTranscriber {
5	
6	    /// Everything a caller may want to SAY about a run that the `Outcome`
7	    /// has no room for — which media were uploaded and what AssemblyAI said
8	    /// about each, which were served from the cache, and what the janitor
9	    /// managed.
10	    ///
11	    /// It is beside the outcome rather than inside it because `Outcome` is
12	    /// the shape BOTH engines answer and the on-device one has nothing to
13	    /// put in any of these fields. The tool reads it for its result keys and
14	    /// c1-chrome's report card reads it for its lines.
15	    struct Report: Equatable {
16	
17	        /// One media this run sent to AssemblyAI, and what came back.
18	        struct Uploaded: Equatable {
19	            let media: UInt32
20	            /// R6-8: which model actually ran, so a fallback is reported.
21	            let speechModelUsed: String?
22	            let languageCode: String?
23	            /// Set when the language was DETECTED, not when it was named.
24	            let languageConfidence: Double?
25	            /// Seconds as AssemblyAI reported them — what was billed.
26	            let audioSeconds: Int
27	            let format: Transcriber.UploadFormat
28	            /// Whether this fetched transcript's initial JSON write landed.
29	            let transcriptWritten: Bool
30	            /// Whether the marker landed. Always false when
31	            /// `transcriptWritten` is: the marker only follows its file.
32	            let stampWritten: Bool
33	            /// Whether the remote transcript is confirmed gone (R6-4).
34	            let remoteDeleted: Bool
35	        }
36	
37	        var uploaded: [Uploaded] = []
38	        /// Media served from `cache/transcripts/` with no request at all.
39	        var cached: [UInt32] = []
40	        /// Media whose earlier transcript the janitor deleted this run.
41	        var janitorDeleted: [UInt32] = []
42	        /// Media whose earlier transcript the janitor could NOT delete.
43	        var janitorFailed: [UInt32] = []
44	        /// Pending remote deletes retained because a keyless run sent no requests.
45	        var janitorDeferred: [UInt32] = []
46	        /// R6-11: in `janitorFailed` AND this run would otherwise have
47	        /// fetched them. A held media is in neither `uploaded` nor `cached`
48	        /// and its clips are reported as problems: its cache file is the one
49	        /// record of an id we still have to delete, and a fetch would
50	        /// overwrite it.
51	        var held: [UInt32] = []
52	        /// Media whose transcript was refused after AssemblyAI made it and
53	        /// whose DELETE answered `failed`. No file holds its id, so it is
54	        /// owed with no retry (R6-20).
55	        var refusedUndeleted: [UInt32] = []
56	
57	        /// What was billed: every uploaded media's `audioSeconds`, the one
58	        /// reducer `AgentServer`'s bill sentence and its `audio_seconds` key
59	        /// both read.
60	        ///
61	        /// SATURATING, because every term is the SERVER's own
62	        /// `audio_duration` and `+` traps: two media answered
63	        /// `9223372036854775807` killed the whole app after both had been
64	        /// uploaded and billed (the reader review, §10.13 R1·1). Each term is
65	        /// floored at 0 first, so the sum only grows and an overflow can only
66	        /// be upward: `Int.max` is sticky, and a later negative term cannot
67	        /// pull a saturated total back down (#187, item 4).
68	        var billedSeconds: Int {
69	            uploaded.reduce(0) { sum, row in
70	                let (total, overflowed) = sum.addingReportingOverflow(max(0, row.audioSeconds))
71	                return overflowed ? Int.max : total
72	            }
73	        }
74	
75	        /// One sentence per uploaded media whose marker did not land, in
76	        /// `uploaded` order (#187, item 2).
77	        ///
78	        /// It states only what `fetch` knows and promises nothing about the
79	        /// next run: on a `refresh` run over a current cache an older file
80	        /// and marker equal to this stamp survive the failed write and are
81	        /// served next time — the rule `AgentServer.billed`'s doc records
82	        /// (issue #29).
83	        func cacheWarnings(name: (UInt32) -> String) -> [String] {
84	            uploaded.filter { !$0.stampWritten }.map {
85	                "The transcript of \(name($0.media)) could not be kept in the project for reuse."
86	            }
87	        }
88	
89	        /// Cleanup still owed, in stable per-media order. An ID can be
90	        /// retried only when its transcript JSON was saved in the project.
91	        func deletionWarnings(name: (UInt32) -> String) -> [String] {
92	            var seen: Set<UInt32> = []
93	            var warnings: [String] = []
94	            func append(_ id: UInt32, written: Bool) {
95	                guard seen.insert(id).inserted else { return }
96	                let target = name(id)
97	                var warning: String
98	                if written {
99	                    warning = "AssemblyAI has not confirmed deleting the transcript of \(target); "
100	                        + "it will be retried at the next run with an API key."
101	                } else {
102	                    warning = "AssemblyAI has not confirmed deleting the transcript of \(target). "
103	                        + "Its transcript could not be saved in the project, so Frame Job cannot "
104	                        + "retry deleting it automatically. Delete it in your AssemblyAI dashboard."
105	                }
106	                if held.contains(id) { warning += " It was not uploaded again in this run." }
107	                warnings.append(warning)
108	            }
109	            for id in janitorFailed { append(id, written: true) }
110	            for id in janitorDeferred where seen.insert(id).inserted {
111	                warnings.append(
112	                    "AssemblyAI has not confirmed deleting the transcript of \(name(id)); "
113	                        + "cleanup was deferred because no API key is set. Its deletion ID is "
114	                        + "retained in the project; a later run with a key for the originating "
115	                        + "account and region will retry deletion only if that ID is safe to send.")
116	            }
117	            for row in uploaded where !row.remoteDeleted {
118	                append(row.media, written: row.transcriptWritten)
119	            }
120	            for id in refusedUndeleted { append(id, written: false) }
121	            return warnings
122	        }
123	    }
124	
125	}

3	/// AssemblyAI's published prices, dated — road map 6 §8's two rows.
4	///
5	/// They are CONSTANTS with a date beside them rather than anything the app
6	/// asks the service for, because AssemblyAI publishes no price endpoint and a
7	/// number invented at run time would be worse than a stale one nobody can
8	/// check. Everything that shows them says "at AssemblyAI's published rate",
9	/// so a figure that has gone stale reads as one.
10	enum AssemblyAIRates {
11	    /// The day the two numbers below were read off AssemblyAI's pricing page.
12	    static let readOn = "2026-09-17"
13	    /// Dollars per hour of audio for Universal-3.5 Pro.
14	    static let perHour = 0.21
15	    /// What speaker labels add, per hour.
16	    static let speakersPerHour = 0.02
17	}
18	
19	/// What a cloud caption run would cost and why — road map 6 §5e's summary
20	/// line, as a PURE value with no run, no client and no sheet in it.
21	///
22	/// **Why it is a type and not four lines inside the sheet.** The estimate is
23	/// the one thing a person sees before agreeing to spend somebody's money and
24	/// to send their audio to another company, and it has to be right about three
25	/// separate things: which files this run would upload, how much audio that is,
26	/// and what that costs. Each of those is a rule with an edge — R6-11 holds a
27	/// media whose earlier delete is unconfirmed, a cached media costs nothing, a
28	/// media whose file will not read costs nothing and transcribes nothing — so
29	/// the arithmetic is a value the probe reads over a table rather than a
30	/// summary somebody typed into a label.
31	///
32	/// **Spec §11's R6-13 is the whole of the awaiting clause.** A held media is
33	/// neither "to upload" (this run will not upload it, and quoting for it would
34	/// quote for work that is not going to happen) nor hidden (a file that
35	/// silently does not transcribe is the failure the clause exists to
36	/// prevent). It is its own count in `describe` and its own line in `reasons`,
37	/// and that line carries what it WOULD cost if the janitor clears the delete.
38	///
39	/// **One disk read, and it is not in this arithmetic.** `facts(jobs:…)` is
40	/// the only member that opens a file: it reads each media's marker, whether
41	/// the transcript itself reads back, and the janitor's list, once per media.
42	/// Everything else — `fate`, `uploadTicks`, `dollars`, `money`, `describe`,
43	/// `reasons` — is a function of those facts, so the sheet can recompute the
44	/// whole readout on every keystroke without touching the disk again.
45	struct CloudEstimate: Equatable {
46	
47	    /// Why a media is not being served from the cache.
48	    enum Reason: Equatable {
49	        /// There is no marker for it, or the transcript beside the marker
50	        /// will not read.
51	        case notCached
52	        /// There IS a transcript, of a file that has changed since.
53	        case fileChanged
54	        /// There is a transcript of this file, of a different REQUEST. The
55	        /// fields are in a fixed order — `model`, `language`, `speakers`,
56	        /// `vocabulary` — so one call's answer is the same sentence every
57	        /// time.
58	        case requestChanged([String])
59	        /// It would have been served from the cache, and Transcribe again
60	        /// was asked for.
61	        case refresh
62	    }
63	
64	    /// What this run would do with one media.
65	    enum Fate: Equatable {
66	        /// Uploaded, and why.
67	        case upload(Reason)
68	        /// Served from `cache/transcripts/`, at no cost at all.
69	        case cached
70	        /// R6-11 will hold it: an earlier remote delete is unconfirmed, so
71	        /// this run leaves it alone. The reason is what it would have been
72	        /// uploaded FOR, which is what makes its price meaningful.
73	        case awaitingDelete(Reason)
74	        /// Its media file could not be read, so nothing can be said about it.
75	        case unreadable
76	    }
77	
78	    /// Everything the disk knows about one media, read once.
79	    struct Facts: Equatable {
80	        let media: UInt32
81	        let name: String
82	        let duration: Ticks
83	        /// The file as it is NOW, or nil when it could not be read at all.
84	        let source: MediaImporter.CacheStamp?
85	        /// `cache/transcripts/<id>.complete.json`, decoded, or nil.
86	        let marker: TranscriptStamp?
87	        /// Whether `cache/transcripts/<id>.json` reads back. Both, because
88	        /// they are separate files — `MediaTranscript.isCurrent`'s rule.
89	        let cacheReads: Bool
90	        /// Whether the janitor still owes AssemblyAI a delete for it.
91	        let deleteOwed: Bool
92	    }
93	
94	    /// One media in the readout.
95	    struct Row: Equatable {
96	        let media: UInt32
97	        let name: String
98	        let duration: Ticks
99	        let fate: Fate
100	    }
101	
102	    /// In the order of each media's FIRST clip, which is the order the run
103	    /// itself works in (`CloudTranscriber.transcribe`'s `order`).
104	    let rows: [Row]
105	    /// Whether speaker labels were asked for, which is what the rate adds to.
106	    let speakers: Bool
107	
108	    init(facts: [Facts], options: TranscriptOptions, refresh: Bool) {
109	        self.rows = facts.map {
110	            Row(
111	                media: $0.media, name: $0.name, duration: $0.duration,
112	                fate: Self.fate($0, options: options, refresh: refresh))
113	        }
114	        self.speakers = options.speakerLabels
115	    }
116	
117	    // MARK: - The facts, and the ONE disk read
118	
119	    /// One `Facts` per media, in first-clip order — the only member of this
120	    /// type that opens a file.
121	    ///
122	    /// It is a static function taking a cache directory rather than anything
123	    /// holding a document, so the sheet reads it once when it opens and the
124	    /// pure arithmetic above runs on every control change.
125	    static func facts(
126	        jobs: [Transcriber.Job], media: [UInt32: MediaSnapshot], cacheDirectory: URL
127	    ) -> [Facts] {
128	        var order: [UInt32] = []
129	        var first: [UInt32: Transcriber.Job] = [:]
130	        for job in jobs where first[job.media] == nil {
131	            order.append(job.media)
132	            first[job.media] = job
133	        }
134	        let owed = Set(MediaTranscript.undeleted(in: cacheDirectory).map { $0.media })
135	        var out: [Facts] = []
136	        for id in order {
137	            guard let job = first[id] else { continue }
138	            let entry = media[id]
139	            let stamp = entry.flatMap { MediaImporter.CacheStamp.stamp(for: $0, url: job.source) }
140	            out.append(
141	                Facts(
142	                    media: id, name: entry?.name ?? job.name, duration: entry?.duration ?? 0,
143	                    source: stamp,
144	                    marker: MediaTranscript.readStamp(for: id, in: cacheDirectory),
145	                    cacheReads: MediaTranscript.read(for: id, in: cacheDirectory) != nil,
146	                    deleteOwed: owed.contains(id)))
147	        }
148	        return out
149	    }
150	
151	    // MARK: - The rules
152	
153	    /// What this run would do with one media — `CloudTranscriber.transcribe`'s
154	    /// own classification, said in the vocabulary a person reads.
155	    ///
156	    /// It is deliberately NOT shared code with the run: the run answers for
157	    /// what it did and this answers for what it would do, and a probe row
158	    /// compares the two so the day they disagree is a scored failure rather
159	    /// than a refactor nobody checked.
160	    static func fate(_ facts: Facts, options: TranscriptOptions, refresh: Bool) -> Fate {
161	        guard let source = facts.source else { return .unreadable }
162	        let wanted = TranscriptStamp(source: source, options: options)
163	        let current = facts.marker?.serves(wanted, for: .captions) == true && facts.cacheReads
164	        if current, !refresh { return .cached }
165	        let reason: Reason
166	        if current {
167	            reason = .refresh
168	        } else if facts.marker == nil || !facts.cacheReads {
169	            reason = .notCached
170	        } else if let marker = facts.marker, marker.source != wanted.source {
171	            reason = .fileChanged
172	        } else {
173	            reason = .requestChanged(changed(facts.marker, wanted))
174	        }
175	        return facts.deleteOwed ? .awaitingDelete(reason) : .upload(reason)
176	    }
177	
178	    /// Which of the request's four parts differ, in the fixed order
179	    /// `model`, `language`, `speakers`, `vocabulary`.
180	    private static func changed(_ marker: TranscriptStamp?, _ wanted: TranscriptStamp) -> [String] {
181	        guard let marker = marker else { return [] }
182	        var out: [String] = []
183	        if marker.speechModels != wanted.speechModels { out.append("model") }
184	        if marker.languageCode != wanted.languageCode { out.append("language") }
185	        if marker.speakerLabels != wanted.speakerLabels { out.append("speakers") }
186	        if marker.keytermsPrompt != wanted.keytermsPrompt { out.append("vocabulary") }
187	        return out
188	    }
189	
190	    // MARK: - The counts
191	
192	    var uploads: [Row] { rows.filter { if case .upload = $0.fate { return true } else { return false } } }
193	    var cached: [Row] { rows.filter { $0.fate == .cached } }
194	    var awaiting: [Row] {
195	        rows.filter { if case .awaitingDelete = $0.fate { return true } else { return false } }
196	    }
197	    var unreadable: [Row] { rows.filter { $0.fate == .unreadable } }
198	
199	    /// A keyless run is admitted only when every distinct media is current.
200	    var canReuseWithoutCredential: Bool {
201	        !rows.isEmpty && rows.allSatisfy { $0.fate == .cached }
202	    }
203	
204	    /// The audio this run would upload, in ticks.
205	    ///
206	    /// Each row is bounded into `[0, Transcriber.maxSourceTicks]` and the sum
207	    /// SATURATES, for that constant's own reason (R6-10): a media's duration
208	    /// comes out of a `project.json` a person can hand-write, and a readout
209	    /// that trapped on one would take the sheet down with it.
210	    var uploadTicks: Ticks {
211	        var total: Ticks = 0
212	        for row in uploads {
213	            let bounded = min(max(row.duration, 0), Transcriber.maxSourceTicks)
214	            let (sum, overflow) = total.addingReportingOverflow(bounded)
215	            total = overflow ? Ticks.max : sum
216	        }
217	        return total
218	    }
219	
220	    // MARK: - The money
221	
222	    /// Ticks of audio at the published rate, in dollars.
223	    static func dollars(ticks: Ticks, speakers: Bool) -> Double {
224	        let hours = Double(max(ticks, 0)) / 600_000 / 3600
225	        return hours * (AssemblyAIRates.perHour + (speakers ? AssemblyAIRates.speakersPerHour : 0))
226	    }
227	
228	    /// `"about $0.36"`, and `"under $0.01"` for anything above nothing that
229	    /// rounds to no cents — quoting "about $0.00" for a run that will be
230	    /// billed is the one wrong answer this function can give.
231	    ///
232	    /// Formatted POSIX, never in the person's locale: this is a dollar figure
233	    /// with a dot in it, and a comma decimal separator would read as
234	    /// thousands.
235	    static func money(_ dollars: Double) -> String {
236	        guard dollars.isFinite else { return "about $0.00" }
237	        let cents = (dollars * 100).rounded()
238	        if dollars > 0, cents < 1 { return "under $0.01" }
239	        return "about $" + amount(max(cents, 0) / 100)
240	    }
241	
242	    private static func amount(_ value: Double) -> String {
243	        String(format: "%.2f", locale: Locale(identifier: "en_US_POSIX"), value)
244	    }
245	
246	    // MARK: - The words
247	
248	    /// §5e's summary line: what would be uploaded, how much audio that is,
249	    /// what it costs, and then each of the three things that cost nothing,
250	    /// named only when there are any.
251	    static func describe(_ estimate: CloudEstimate, fps: Fps) -> String {
252	        guard !estimate.rows.isEmpty else { return "Nothing to transcribe" }
253	        var parts: [String] = []
254	        let uploads = estimate.uploads.count
255	        if uploads == 0 {
256	            parts.append("Nothing to upload")
257	        } else {
258	            parts.append("\(uploads) \(files(uploads)) to upload")
259	            parts.append(
260	                ReelTime.format(estimate.uploadTicks, fps: fps, frames: false) + " of audio")
261	            parts.append(
262	                money(dollars(ticks: estimate.uploadTicks, speakers: estimate.speakers))
263	                    + " at AssemblyAI's published rate")
264	        }
265	        let cached = estimate.cached.count
266	        if cached > 0 { parts.append("\(cached) \(files(cached)) already transcribed") }
267	        let awaiting = estimate.awaiting.count
268	        if awaiting > 0 {
269	            parts.append("\(awaiting) \(files(awaiting)) waiting on an earlier delete")
270	        }
271	        let unreadable = estimate.unreadable.count
272	        if unreadable > 0 { parts.append("\(unreadable) \(files(unreadable)) could not be read") }
273	        return parts.joined(separator: " · ")
274	    }
275	
276	    private static func files(_ count: Int) -> String { count == 1 ? "file" : "files" }
277	
278	    /// One line per row that is not being served from the cache, by FILE
279	    /// NAME, and then the rate sentence.
280	    ///
281	    /// By name rather than by media id because the person chose files, not
282	    /// ids, and an id is the tool's vocabulary. R6-13: an awaiting row's line
283	    /// says what it would cost if the delete clears, so its price is never
284	    /// hidden by the count that leaves it out of the total.
285	    static func reasons(_ estimate: CloudEstimate) -> [String] {
286	        var out: [String] = []
287	        for row in estimate.rows {
288	            switch row.fate {
289	            case .cached:
290	                continue
291	            case .unreadable:
292	                out.append("“\(row.name)” could not be read, so it cannot be transcribed.")
293	            case .upload(let reason):
294	                out.append(sentence(row, reason))
295	            case .awaitingDelete(let reason):
296	                let bounded = min(max(row.duration, 0), Transcriber.maxSourceTicks)
297	                let price = money(dollars(ticks: bounded, speakers: estimate.speakers))
298	                out.append(
299	                    sentence(row, reason)
300	                        + " It is waiting on an earlier delete and will not be uploaded in this "
301	                        + "run — \(price) more if it does.")
302	            }
303	        }
304	        if !out.isEmpty { out.append(rateSentence(speakers: estimate.speakers)) }
305	        return out
306	    }
307	
308	    private static func sentence(_ row: Row, _ reason: Reason) -> String {
309	        switch reason {
310	        case .notCached:
311	            return "“\(row.name)” has not been transcribed yet."
312	        case .fileChanged:
313	            return "“\(row.name)” has changed since it was transcribed."
314	        case .requestChanged(let fields):
315	            guard !fields.isEmpty else {
316	                return "“\(row.name)” was transcribed for a different request."
317	            }
318	            return "“\(row.name)” was transcribed with a different "
319	                + fields.joined(separator: ", ") + "."
320	        case .refresh:
321	            return "“\(row.name)” is already transcribed, and Transcribe again was asked for."
322	        }
323	    }
324	
325	    /// The dated rate, in one sentence, with the speakers surcharge folded in
326	    /// when it applies — so the figure named here is the figure the total was
327	    /// computed from.
328	    static func rateSentence(speakers: Bool) -> String {
329	        let rate = AssemblyAIRates.perHour + (speakers ? AssemblyAIRates.speakersPerHour : 0)
330	        return "At AssemblyAI's published rate of $\(amount(rate)) an hour, read on "
331	            + "\(AssemblyAIRates.readOn)."
332	    }
333	}

3	/// The two things that make an AssemblyAI client, resolved in one place: WHERE
4	/// it speaks (the base URL) and WHAT it says it is (the credential). R6-6 —
5	/// the protocol boundary is exactly this pair, so the stand-in server of road
6	/// map 6 §5i, the EU endpoint and a same-protocol relay are configurations
7	/// and not code.
8	///
9	/// **R6-9, the rule this file is the whole of.** A proof-launched app must
10	/// never open the person's stored key. `-RCSecretFolder <path>` overrides the
11	/// store's folder; with `-RCAssemblyAIEndpoint` set and no `-RCSecretFolder`,
12	/// NO `FileStore` is built at all and `store()` answers an empty
13	/// `MemoryStore`, so an app pointed at a stand-in has the environment as its
14	/// only credential. Both arguments are read ONLY out of the ARGUMENT domain,
15	/// so a persisted default — `UserDefaults`, a plist somebody wrote, a
16	/// leftover from another session — can redirect neither. Without that rule a
17	/// machine where the person had saved a real key would send it to a server
18	/// that writes every header to disk.
19	///
20	/// **`AppSupport.directory` is touched in exactly one line of this file** and
21	/// nowhere else in the feature, which is what makes "no proof reads the real
22	/// folder" checkable by reading rather than by hoping.
23	enum AssemblyAIConfiguration {
24	
25	    /// The endpoint override, the `-RCRecordingFolder` idiom
26	    /// (`RecordingSetup.swift`). A whole base URL rather than a host, because
27	    /// the scheme is part of what is being overridden: the stand-in speaks
28	    /// plain HTTP.
29	    static let endpointArgument = "RCAssemblyAIEndpoint"
30	
31	    /// The store-folder override (R6-9). A PATH, never a key — `ps` shows
32	    /// every launch argument to every user on the machine, which is the same
33	    /// reason R6-5 keeps the credential out of `transcribe`'s arguments.
34	    static let secretFolderArgument = "RCSecretFolder"
35	
36	    /// The persisted region, the Settings window's popup.
37	    static let regionKey = "FrameJobAssemblyAIRegion"
38	
39	    /// The environment override, read only when the store has nothing
40	    /// (R6-5, R6-9 (d)).
41	    static let environmentKey = "RC_ASSEMBLYAI_KEY"
42	
43	    /// AssemblyAI's two data regions (road map 6 §2). A transcript made in
44	    /// one is not visible in the other, which is why this is a setting and
45	    /// not a fallback.
46	    enum Region: String, CaseIterable {
47	        case us
48	        case eu
49	
50	        var base: URL {
51	            switch self {
52	            case .us: return Region.url("https://api.assemblyai.com")
53	            case .eu: return Region.url("https://api.eu.assemblyai.com")
54	            }
55	        }
56	
57	        /// `URL(string:)` is optional because its input is usually somebody
58	        /// else's; these two are literals on the lines above. A parse that
59	        /// failed would be a typo there, and the fallback reaches no host at
60	        /// all — every request against it refuses, which is the safe
61	        /// direction: never a DIFFERENT server.
62	        private static func url(_ text: String) -> URL {
63	            URL(string: text) ?? URL(fileURLWithPath: "/dev/null")
64	        }
65	
66	        var displayName: String {
67	            switch self {
68	            case .us: return "United States"
69	            case .eu: return "European Union"
70	            }
71	        }
72	    }
73	
74	    /// Why a configured endpoint cannot be used, in a sentence the Settings
75	    /// window and a tool can both print.
76	    enum ConfigurationError: LocalizedError, Equatable {
77	        case malformedEndpoint(String)
78	        case insecureEndpoint(String)
79	
80	        var errorDescription: String? {
81	            switch self {
82	            case .malformedEndpoint(let text):
83	                return "“\(text)” is not a URL the transcription service can be reached at."
84	            case .insecureEndpoint(let host):
85	                return "A plain HTTP endpoint is only allowed for a local server, and "
86	                    + "“\(host)” is not one."
87	            }
88	        }
89	    }
90	
91	    /// The region the person chose. An unknown or absent value is `.us`, not
92	    /// an error: a defaults file written by a later build, or by hand, must
93	    /// not stop the app from transcribing.
94	    static func region(defaults: UserDefaults = .standard) -> Region {
95	        guard let raw = defaults.string(forKey: regionKey), let region = Region(rawValue: raw)
96	        else { return .us }
97	        return region
98	    }
99	
100	    /// Where the client speaks: the argument-domain endpoint when one is set,
101	    /// the region's own host otherwise.
102	    static func baseURL(defaults: UserDefaults = .standard) throws -> URL {
103	        guard let override = argument(endpointArgument, defaults: defaults) else {
104	            return region(defaults: defaults).base
105	        }
106	        guard let url = URL(string: override), let scheme = url.scheme?.lowercased(),
107	            let host = url.host, !host.isEmpty
108	        else { throw ConfigurationError.malformedEndpoint(override) }
109	        guard scheme == "http" || scheme == "https" else {
110	            throw ConfigurationError.malformedEndpoint(override)
111	        }
112	        // Plain HTTP for a loopback host only. C0's q3 measured that macOS
113	        // 26.5.1 does not block it from an ad-hoc-signed hardened-runtime
114	        // bundle with no ATS key at all, which is why `project.yml` carries
115	        // none — and this guard is what keeps that measurement from becoming
116	        // a licence to send a key over the open network in clear.
117	        guard scheme == "https" || isLoopback(host) else {
118	            throw ConfigurationError.insecureEndpoint(host)
119	        }
120	        return url
121	    }
122	
123	    /// The `SecretStore` this process may use, and R6-9's whole decision in
124	    /// one function.
125	    ///
126	    /// With `-RCSecretFolder` set, a `FileStore` on that folder: a proof's
127	    /// own disposable directory. With no `-RCSecretFolder` but
128	    /// `-RCAssemblyAIEndpoint` set, an EMPTY `MemoryStore`: the app has been
129	    /// pointed at something that is not AssemblyAI, so the person's stored
130	    /// key is not opened at all and `RC_ASSEMBLYAI_KEY` is the only
131	    /// credential such a run can have. With neither, the person's own file
132	    /// under `AppSupport.directory` — the ONE line in this feature that names
133	    /// it. A machine with no Application Support folder answers an empty
134	    /// `MemoryStore` too, which reads as "no key is set".
135	    static func store(defaults: UserDefaults = .standard) -> any SecretStore {
136	        if let folder = argument(secretFolderArgument, defaults: defaults) {
137	            return FileStore(
138	                directory: URL(
139	                    fileURLWithPath: (folder as NSString).expandingTildeInPath,
140	                    isDirectory: true))
141	        }
142	        if argument(endpointArgument, defaults: defaults) != nil { return MemoryStore() }
143	        guard let directory = AppSupport.directory else { return MemoryStore() }
144	        return FileStore(directory: directory)
145	    }
146	
147	    /// The credential: the store first, the environment second (R6-5, and
148	    /// R6-9 (d) amends the wording of that order and not the order). An empty
149	    /// environment variable is no credential, for `FileStore.read`'s reason.
150	    static func credential(
151	        store: any SecretStore,
152	        environment: [String: String] = ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment
153	    ) -> String? {
154	        if let stored = store.read() { return stored }
155	        guard let value = environment[environmentKey] else { return nil }
156	        let trimmed = value.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
157	        return trimmed.isEmpty ? nil : trimmed
158	    }
159	
160	    /// The three spellings of this machine, and only those three.
161	    /// `localhost.evil.com` resolves wherever its owner says and is not one
162	    /// of them; a bracketed IPv6 literal arrives from `URL.host` without its
163	    /// brackets, which is why `::1` is compared bare.
164	    static func isLoopback(_ host: String) -> Bool {
165	        let name = host.lowercased()
166	        return name == "127.0.0.1" || name == "localhost" || name == "::1"
167	    }
168	
169	    /// A launch argument, from the ARGUMENT domain alone (R6-9 (c)). Reading
170	    /// it off `UserDefaults.standard.string(forKey:)` would let a value
171	    /// persisted in the app's own plist — by a previous session, by an
172	    /// installer, by anything running as the person — move where the key is
173	    /// read from, which is exactly what this rule forbids. Empty is absent.
174	    static func argument(_ key: String, defaults: UserDefaults) -> String? {
175	        let domain = defaults.volatileDomain(forName: UserDefaults.argumentDomain)
176	        guard let value = domain[key] as? String, !value.isEmpty else { return nil }
177	        return value
178	    }
179	}

3	/// The cloud run's one number, and the words beside it — road map 6 §5a's
4	/// progress paragraph as a value with no run in it.
5	///
6	/// **Why a type and not four lines inside the run.** The bar is the only
7	/// thing a person watching a cloud transcription has to go on: a run is
8	/// minutes of somebody else's compute and nothing about it is visible
9	/// otherwise. A number that went backwards, or that reached 0.95 and sat
10	/// there for a media that had not started, would be read as a hang. So the
11	/// arithmetic is pure, takes no client, no file and no clock of its own, and
12	/// is measured by `cloud_captions_probe.py`'s section `run` against a table
13	/// — the sheet that shows it in c1-chrome inherits something proved rather
14	/// than something plausible.
15	///
16	/// **The shares.** A run uploads one media at a time, so its bar is the
17	/// media's own progress scaled into that media's slice of the whole, and the
18	/// slices are proportional to the SECONDS of audio each media carries —
19	/// which is the only number known before any work is done and is very nearly
20	/// proportional to every phase's cost (the extract reads it, the upload
21	/// sends a fixed rate of it, the wait is §3 q8's 147× of it). A media that
22	/// is served from the cache, and a media R6-11 HOLDS, are not in the list at
23	/// all: they cost nothing and a slice for them would make the bar stall.
24	///
25	/// Inside one media's slice the four phases divide it exactly as §5a says:
26	/// extraction 0–0.25, upload 0.25–0.65, the wait 0.65–0.95 and the write to
27	/// 1.0. The wait is the only one with no honest completion signal — a poll
28	/// answers `processing` or it does not — so it advances on the CLOCK against
29	/// q8's measured 147× real time and HOLDS at 0.95 rather than pretending to
30	/// finish. The submit, between the upload and the wait, has no span of its
31	/// own: it is one request whose only progress is its answer, so it holds at
32	/// the upload's end, 0.65, with a detail line of its own naming the file.
33	struct CloudProgress {
34	
35	    /// Where one media is in its own slice.
36	    enum Phase: Equatable {
37	        case extracting
38	        case uploading
39	        case submitting
40	        case waiting
41	        case saving
42	    }
43	
44	    /// §5a's four boundaries, and q8's rate. `processingRate` is audio
45	    /// seconds transcribed per second of wall clock: C0 measured an hour
46	    /// completing in 24.4 s.
47	    static let extractEnd = 0.25
48	    static let uploadEnd = 0.65
49	    static let waitEnd = 0.95
50	    static let processingRate = 147.0
51	
52	    /// Each media's slice, in run order, summing to 1. Empty when nothing is
53	    /// being uploaded, which is the cached-only run: its bar goes 0 → 1.
54	    private let shares: [Double]
55	    /// Where each slice begins.
56	    private let bases: [Double]
57	
58	    /// `seconds` is one entry per media TO UPLOAD, in the order the run will
59	    /// do them. A total of zero — every media a zero-length extract — falls
60	    /// back to equal slices rather than dividing by it.
61	    init(seconds: [Double]) {
62	        let clean = seconds.map { $0.isFinite && $0 > 0 ? $0 : 0 }
63	        let total = clean.reduce(0, +)
64	        if clean.isEmpty {
65	            shares = []
66	        } else if total > 0 {
67	            shares = clean.map { $0 / total }
68	        } else {
69	            shares = clean.map { _ in 1 / Double(clean.count) }
70	        }
71	        var running = 0.0
72	        var starts: [Double] = []
73	        for share in shares {
74	            starts.append(running)
75	            running += share
76	        }
77	        bases = starts
78	    }
79	
80	    /// The whole run's fraction while media `index` is `within` its `phase`.
81	    ///
82	    /// `within` is clamped into 0…1 — a phase reports its own completion and
83	    /// a caller that measured 1.4 of an upload is not allowed to move the
84	    /// bar past the media's slice. An index outside the list answers 0,
85	    /// which is also what a run with nothing to upload answers: neither has
86	    /// a slice to be inside.
87	    func fraction(media index: Int, phase: Phase, within: Double) -> Double {
88	        guard index >= 0, index < shares.count else { return 0 }
89	        let part = within.isNaN ? 0 : min(max(within, 0), 1)
90	        let span: (Double, Double)
91	        switch phase {
92	        case .extracting: span = (0, Self.extractEnd)
93	        case .uploading: span = (Self.extractEnd, Self.uploadEnd)
94	        case .submitting: span = (Self.uploadEnd, Self.uploadEnd)
95	        case .waiting: span = (Self.uploadEnd, Self.waitEnd)
96	        case .saving: span = (Self.waitEnd, 1)
97	        }
98	        // The two ends are taken EXACTLY rather than computed: with one
99	        // media `0.65 + (0.95 − 0.65) × 1` is 0.9500000000000001 in binary
100	        // floating point, and "holds at 0.95" is a claim a proof compares
101	        // against the constant.
102	        let value = part >= 1 ? span.1 : (part <= 0 ? span.0 : span.0 + (span.1 - span.0) * part)
103	        return bases[index] + shares[index] * value
104	    }
105	
106	    /// How far through the WAIT a media is, by the clock: `waited × 147`
107	    /// audio seconds' worth of somebody else's compute, over the audio there
108	    /// is. Capped at 1, which is where §5a's "holds at 0.95" comes from —
109	    /// this is the `within`, and 1 of the wait is 0.95 of the slice.
110	    ///
111	    /// Audio of zero or less answers 1: there is nothing to wait for and a
112	    /// division would be the wrong kind of infinity.
113	    static func waiting(waited: TimeInterval, audioSeconds: Double) -> Double {
114	        guard audioSeconds.isFinite, audioSeconds > 0 else { return 1 }
115	        guard waited.isFinite, waited > 0 else { return 0 }
116	        return min(1, waited * processingRate / audioSeconds)
117	    }
118	
119	    /// §5a's detail line — the phase and the file, plus the megabytes for an
120	    /// upload and the seconds for a wait, so a stuck queue is visible rather
121	    /// than silent. Five lines: the submit names its file too.
122	    ///
123	    /// Megabytes are 1 000 000 bytes, the unit a service's own dashboard
124	    /// counts in, and they are whole numbers: a tenth of a megabyte moving
125	    /// once a second is noise, not information. A count under one megabyte
126	    /// is `<1`, never a 0 or a 1 it is not, so a small file's upload does
127	    /// not read `0 MB of 0`.
128	    static func detail(
129	        _ phase: Phase, file: String, sent: Int64 = 0, total: Int64 = 0,
130	        waited: TimeInterval = 0
131	    ) -> String {
132	        switch phase {
133	        case .extracting:
134	            return "Extracting \(file)"
135	        case .uploading:
136	            return "Uploading \(file) · \(megabytes(sent)) MB of \(megabytes(total))"
137	        case .submitting:
138	            return "Submitting \(file)"
139	        case .waiting:
140	            return "Waiting for AssemblyAI · \(Int(max(0, waited.rounded()))) s"
141	        case .saving:
142	            return "Saving \(file)"
143	        }
144	    }
145	
146	    private static func megabytes(_ bytes: Int64) -> String {
147	        if bytes <= 0 { return "0" }
148	        if bytes < 1_000_000 { return "<1" }
149	        return String(Int((Double(bytes) / 1_000_000).rounded()))
150	    }
151	}

1	import Foundation

3	/// The cloud engine's seam and its run: `TranscriptionEngine`, the two
4	/// spellings a caption run can be asked for, and `CloudTranscriber`, which
5	/// takes exactly what `Transcriber` takes and answers exactly what
6	/// `Transcriber` answers — road map 6 §5a, whole.
7	///
8	/// **What a run is.** The janitor first (R6-4), then the jobs grouped by
9	/// MEDIA rather than by clip, because R6-3 says one upload per media file and
10	/// every clip over it is derived from that one transcript. A media whose
11	/// cache is current is read from disk and costs no request at all; a media
12	/// whose remote delete this run could not confirm is HELD (R6-11); every
13	/// other media is extracted whole, uploaded, submitted, polled, written to
14	/// the cache and deleted remotely, in that order. Then each job's words are
15	/// cut out of its media's transcript by the mapping and built into cues.
16	///
17	/// **One media's failure is one media's problem.** `Transcriber`'s rule, read
18	/// across: a media that could not be transcribed is reported under
19	/// `problems` for every clip on it and the run carries on, because a run is a
20	/// LIST and throwing away the media that worked over the one that did not is
21	/// minutes of somebody else's compute discarded. There are exactly two
22	/// exceptions and both are named in §5a: a CANCELLATION, which is the
23	/// person's instruction to place nothing, and a REFUSED KEY, which would fail
24	/// every later media the same way and cost an upload each time it did.
25	///
26	/// **`run` is `Transcriber.run`'s twin line for line.** R6-7: no `async`
27	/// here or below it, one serial queue, the body synchronous on it, the single
28	/// completion posted to main.
29	enum TranscriptionEngine: String, CaseIterable {
30	    /// On-device `SpeechTranscriber` — `Transcriber`, the default.
31	    case apple
32	    /// AssemblyAI over the network — `CloudTranscriber`.
33	    case assemblyai
34	
35	    /// What the sheet remembers between opens (road map 6 §5a). An agent call
36	    /// never reads it: R6-2 says the cloud engine is asked for every time.
37	    static let defaultsKey = "FrameJobCaptionEngine"
38	
39	    /// The popup's words. "On this Mac" rather than "Apple" because what the
40	    /// person is choosing is where their audio goes, not whose recogniser it
41	    /// is.
42	    var displayName: String {
43	        switch self {
44	        case .apple: return "On this Mac"
45	        case .assemblyai: return "AssemblyAI"
46	        }
47	    }
48	}
49	
50	/// AssemblyAI as a second engine behind the one command (R6-1). Same jobs,
51	/// same cancel token, same frame, same `Outcome`, so
52	/// `TranscribeSheetController.finish` and the tool's placement code cannot
53	/// tell which engine ran.
54	final class CloudTranscriber {
55	
56	    enum AccessError: LocalizedError, Equatable {
57	        case credentialRequired
58	
59	        var errorDescription: String? {
60	            ModelKeys.sentence(.assemblyAI)
61	        }
62	    }
63	
64	    /// The serial queue the whole run happens on — `Transcriber.work`'s
65	    /// twin, and one of the queue seams app/CLAUDE.md lists. A run is
66	    /// network-bound minutes of somebody else's compute and must never be on
67	    /// main.
68	    private let work = DispatchQueue(label: "com.kgalligan.framejob.cloud-transcribe")
69	
70	    let client: AssemblyAIClient?
71	    /// Where `cache/transcripts/` lives for this run — the document's cache
72	    /// directory, passed by value so the run holds no document.
73	    let cacheDirectory: URL
74	    /// The media records the jobs point at, by id, for the stamp.
75	    let media: [UInt32: MediaSnapshot]
76	
77	    /// What the last run said. Written only inside `transcribe`, read only
78	    /// after it returns (or after `run`'s completion has fired), which is why
79	    /// it needs no lock: one run at a time on one serial queue, and the
80	    /// caller that reads it is the caller that waited for it.
81	    private(set) var report = Report()
82	
83	    init(client: AssemblyAIClient? = nil, cacheDirectory: URL, media: [UInt32: MediaSnapshot]) {
84	        self.client = client
85	        self.cacheDirectory = cacheDirectory
86	        self.media = media
87	    }
88	
89	    /// Transcribes every job and answers on the MAIN thread —
90	    /// `Transcriber.run`'s seam, so a sheet and a semaphore-waiting tool can
91	    /// both stay synchronous. `progress` is NOT hopped: it fires on the run's
92	    /// own queue and its caller bounces it.
93	    func run(
94	        jobs: [Transcriber.Job], options: TranscriptOptions, refresh: Bool, frame: Ticks,
95	        pages: CaptionPages.Request, cancel: Transcriber.CancelToken,
96	        progress: ((Double, String) -> Void)? = nil,
97	        completion: @escaping (Result<Transcriber.Outcome, any Error>) -> Void
98	    ) {
99	        work.async { [weak self] in
100	            guard let self = self else { return }
101	            let outcome = Result {
102	                try self.transcribe(
103	                    jobs, options: options, refresh: refresh, frame: frame, pages: pages,
104	                    cancel: cancel, progress: progress)
105	            }
106	            DispatchQueue.main.async { completion(outcome) }
107	        }
108	    }
109	
110	    /// `GET /v2/transcript?limit=1` on the run's OWN queue, answered on
111	    /// main — the Settings window's Verify button.
112	    ///
113	    /// Spec §11's R6-12: verify adds no queue. `work` is already one of the
114	    /// seams `app/CLAUDE.md` lists, and a second one for a single cheap
115	    /// authenticated GET would be a queue nobody could name a rule for.
116	    ///
117	    /// It captures the CLIENT and not `self`. A verify is a wait on a socket
118	    /// and the window that asked may be gone before it answers; there is
119	    /// nothing on this object for it to write, and a strong `self` would
120	    /// keep a whole transcriber alive for the duration of a button press.
121	    func verify(completion: @escaping (Result<Void, AssemblyAIClient.ClientError>) -> Void) {
122	        guard let client = self.client else {
123	            DispatchQueue.main.async {
124	                completion(.failure(.request(AccessError.credentialRequired.localizedDescription)))
125	            }
126	            return
127	        }
128	        work.async {
129	            let answer = client.verify()
130	            DispatchQueue.main.async { completion(answer) }
131	        }
132	    }
133	
134	    /// The synchronous body, road map 6 §5a. Call it off the main thread; a
135	    /// tool that already runs on the server thread calls it directly.
136	    ///
137	    /// There is no ceiling to report on the other side of a REST call, and
138	    /// since W2 there is none on this Mac either (spec §11 W-8): the tool's
139	    /// `truncated` key is gone for both engines, and the proof says so.
140	    func transcribe(
141	        _ jobs: [Transcriber.Job], options: TranscriptOptions, refresh: Bool, frame: Ticks,
142	        pages: CaptionPages.Request, cancel: Transcriber.CancelToken,
143	        progress: ((Double, String) -> Void)? = nil
144	    ) throws -> Transcriber.Outcome {
145	        report = Report()
146	        var last = 0.0
147	        func publish(_ value: Double, _ detail: String) {
148	            last = max(last, value)
149	            progress?(last, detail)
150	        }
151	        publish(0, "")
152	
153	        // (1) The janitor, FIRST on keyed runs — before anything this run does can
154	        // overwrite the file that holds an id we still owe a DELETE. A Stop
155	        // the person has ALREADY pressed is answered above it, and one that
156	        // arrives during it is heard between its items (the reader review,
157	        // §10.13 R1·2).
158	        if cancel.isCancelled { throw Transcriber.TranscribeError.cancelled }
159	        if client == nil {
160	            report.janitorDeferred = MediaTranscript.undeleted(in: cacheDirectory).map(\.media)
161	        } else {
162	            let janitor = retryDeletes(cancel: cancel)
163	            report.janitorDeleted = janitor.deleted
164	            report.janitorFailed = janitor.failed
165	        }
166	        if cancel.isCancelled { throw Transcriber.TranscribeError.cancelled }
167	        if client == nil, jobs.isEmpty || refresh { throw AccessError.credentialRequired }
168	
169	        // (2) Grouped by media, in the order of each media's FIRST clip, and
170	        // classified before any work starts so the progress shares are known.
171	        var order: [UInt32] = []
172	        var grouped: [UInt32: [Transcriber.Job]] = [:]
173	        for job in jobs {
174	            if grouped[job.media] == nil { order.append(job.media) }
175	            grouped[job.media, default: []].append(job)
176	        }
177	        // Admit the entire keyless batch from disk before deriving a cue.
178	        // Holding these decoded files also closes the gap between admission
179	        // and use if a package file disappears while the worker is running.
180	        var keylessFiles: [UInt32: MediaTranscript.File] = [:]
181	        if client == nil {
182	            for id in order {
183	                if cancel.isCancelled { throw Transcriber.TranscribeError.cancelled }
184	                guard let entry = media[id], let url = grouped[id]?.first?.source,
185	                    let source = MediaImporter.CacheStamp.stamp(for: entry, url: url),
186	                    MediaTranscript.readStamp(for: id, in: cacheDirectory)?.serves(
187	                        TranscriptStamp(source: source, options: options), for: .captions) == true,
188	                    let file = MediaTranscript.read(for: id, in: cacheDirectory)
189	                else { throw AccessError.credentialRequired }
190	                keylessFiles[id] = file
191	            }
192	            report.cached = order
193	        }
194	        var stamps: [UInt32: TranscriptStamp] = [:]
195	        var unreadable: [UInt32] = []
196	        var toUpload: [UInt32] = []
197	        var held: [UInt32] = []
198	        var cached: [UInt32] = []
199	        for id in order {
200	            if client == nil { continue }
201	            guard let entry = media[id], let url = grouped[id]?.first?.source,
202	                let source = MediaImporter.CacheStamp.stamp(for: entry, url: url)
203	            else {
204	                unreadable.append(id)
205	                continue
206	            }
207	            let stamp = TranscriptStamp(source: source, options: options)
208	            stamps[id] = stamp
209	            if MediaTranscript.isCurrent(stamp, for: id, in: cacheDirectory), !refresh {
210	                cached.append(id)
211	            } else if report.janitorFailed.contains(id) {
212	                held.append(id)
213	            } else {
214	                toUpload.append(id)
215	            }
216	        }
217	        report.held = held
218	        // Held and cached media are NOT in the shares: neither costs a
219	        // second of work, and a slice for one would make the bar stall.
220	        let bar = CloudProgress(seconds: toUpload.map { ReelTime.seconds(media[$0]?.duration ?? 0) })
221	
222	        var files: [UInt32: MediaTranscript.File] = [:]
223	        var cues: [CaptionLayout.Cue] = []
224	        var problems: [CaptionLayout.Problem] = []
225	        var clips: [UInt32] = []
226	        // Kept apart from `problems` for `Transcriber.transcribe`'s reason:
227	        // they decide WHICH refusal an empty run earns.
228	        var failures: [String] = []
229	
230	        func refuse(_ id: UInt32, _ reason: String) {
231	            for job in grouped[id] ?? [] {
232	                problems.append(CaptionLayout.Problem(tag: "clip \(job.clip)", reason: reason))
233	                failures.append("clip \(job.clip): \(reason)")
234	            }
235	        }
236	
237	        for id in order {
238	            if cancel.isCancelled { throw Transcriber.TranscribeError.cancelled }
239	            if let file = keylessFiles[id] {
240	                files[id] = file
241	            } else if unreadable.contains(id) {
242	                refuse(id, "its media file could not be read")
243	            } else if cached.contains(id) {
244	                if let file = MediaTranscript.read(for: id, in: cacheDirectory) {
245	                    files[id] = file
246	                    report.cached.append(id)
247	                } else {
248	                    refuse(id, "its cached transcript could not be read")
249	                }
250	            } else if held.contains(id) {
251	                // R6-11, the whole of it: no fetch, no write, one sentence
252	                // per clip, and the file left byte for byte.
253	                refuse(
254	                    id,
255	                    "AssemblyAI has not confirmed deleting its earlier transcript, so it was "
256	                        + "not uploaded again; the next run with an API key retries the delete")
257	            } else if let index = toUpload.firstIndex(of: id), let entry = media[id],
258	                let url = grouped[id]?.first?.source, let stamp = stamps[id]
259	            {
260	                do {
261	                    let answer = try fetch(
262	                        media: entry, url: url, stamp: stamp, options: options, cancel: cancel,
263	                        progress: { phase, within, detail in
264	                            publish(bar.fraction(media: index, phase: phase, within: within), detail)
265	                        })
266	                    files[id] = answer.file
267	                    report.uploaded.append(answer.uploaded)
268	                    publish(
269	                        bar.fraction(media: index, phase: .saving, within: 1),
270	                        CloudProgress.detail(.saving, file: entry.name))
271	                } catch {
272	                    // R6-20: a transcript refused after it was made, whose
273	                    // DELETE failed, is owed with no file to retry it from;
274	                    // everything below reads the refusal's own `ClientError`.
275	                    let refusal = error as? AssemblyAIClient.Refusal
276	                    if refusal?.deletion == .failed { report.refusedUndeleted.append(id) }
277	                    let error: any Error = refusal?.failure ?? error
278	                    if let client = error as? AssemblyAIClient.ClientError,
279	                        case .submissionUnresolved(let authenticationStatus) = client,
280	                        cancel.isCancelled || authenticationStatus != nil
281	                    {
282	                        throw client
283	                    }
284	                    if cancel.isCancelled { throw Transcriber.TranscribeError.cancelled }
285	                    if let client = error as? AssemblyAIClient.ClientError {
286	                        if client == .cancelled { throw Transcriber.TranscribeError.cancelled }
287	                        // An auth failure ends the run at once: every later
288	                        // media would fail the same way and each costs an
289	                        // upload to find out.
290	                        if case .keyRefused = client { throw error }
291	                    }
292	                    if let native = error as? Transcriber.TranscribeError, native == .cancelled {
293	                        throw Transcriber.TranscribeError.cancelled
294	                    }
295	                    refuse(id, error.localizedDescription)
296	                }
297	            }
298	
299	            // (4) Every job on this media, derived from the one transcript.
300	            guard let file = files[id] else { continue }
301	            for job in grouped[id] ?? [] {
302	                let words = MediaTranscript.captionWords(for: job, in: file)
303	                    .filter { $0.start < job.start + job.duration }
304	                cues.append(
305	                    contentsOf: CaptionPages.cues(
306	                        from: words, span: job.span, frame: frame, request: pages,
307	                        engine: .assemblyai, clip: job.clip, media: job.media))
308	                if words.isEmpty {
309	                    problems.append(
310	                        CaptionLayout.Problem(
311	                            tag: "clip \(job.clip)", reason: "no speech was recognised in it"))
312	                } else {
313	                    clips.append(job.clip)
314	                }
315	            }
316	        }
317	
318	        if cancel.isCancelled { throw Transcriber.TranscribeError.cancelled }
319	        guard !cues.isEmpty else {
320	            // `Transcriber.transcribe`'s two closing throws, same rule: "no
321	            // speech was recognised" is a claim about the AUDIO, and making
322	            // it when the audio was never read would send somebody looking
323	            // for words that are on the timeline.
324	            guard failures.isEmpty else {
325	                throw Transcriber.TranscribeError.failed(
326	                    failures.prefix(3).joined(separator: "; "))
327	            }
328	            throw Transcriber.TranscribeError.nothingRecognized
329	        }
330	        publish(1, "")
331	        return Transcriber.Outcome(cues: cues, problems: problems, clips: clips)
332	    }
333	}

1	import Foundation
2	
3	/// The two halves of a cloud run that are about ONE media file: the janitor,
4	/// which is the run's first act, and the round trip, which is everything
5	/// between "this media is not cached" and "its words are on disk".
6	///
7	/// They are here rather than in `CloudTranscriber.swift` because that file
8	/// holds the run's SHAPE — the janitor, the grouping, the classification, the
9	/// per-job derivation and the two closing throws — and a reader following
10	/// that shape does not need the header's twelve fields or the order of the
11	/// five calls in front of them. Both files are under the 400-line cap a new
12	/// file has (app/CLAUDE.md, road map 6 §5h).
13	extension CloudTranscriber {
14	
15	    /// Why one media could not be sent, in a sentence with no prefix on it.
16	    ///
17	    /// `Transcriber.TranscribeError.failed` would wrap this in "The
18	    /// transcription failed: ", which is true of the run and not of the
19	    /// media, and the refusal has to name the FILE and the limit — road map
20	    /// 6 §5g puts the ten-hour refusal above the network for exactly that
21	    /// reason: it is knowable before a byte is extracted, let alone sent.
22	    enum MediaError: LocalizedError, Equatable {
23	        case tooLong(String)
24	
25	        var errorDescription: String? {
26	            switch self {
27	            case .tooLong(let name):
28	                return "“\(name)” is longer than AssemblyAI's 10-hour limit for one file."
29	            }
30	        }
31	    }
32	
33	    // MARK: - The janitor
34	
35	    /// R6-4's first act: every cached transcript whose remote copy this app
36	    /// has not managed to delete gets its DELETE retried, best effort, on
37	    /// `deleteTimeout` each.
38	    ///
39	    /// A success rewrites that one flag and nothing else —
40	    /// `MediaTranscript.File`'s header is mutated and written back through
41	    /// the same door, so the served `words` bytes are spliced through
42	    /// untouched and the file is never re-serialised. A failure is REPORTED
43	    /// rather than swallowed, because R6-11 makes it mean something: the run
44	    /// will not fetch that media at all, since this file is the one record of
45	    /// the id still owed a delete.
46	    ///
47	    /// A repeat DELETE of an already-deleted transcript answers 200 (C0's
48	    /// q6), so a retry can never make things worse.
49	    ///
50	    /// **A Stop is heard BETWEEN items.** `cancel` is optional and defaulted
51	    /// so `retryDeletes()` still means what it always did, but a run that has
52	    /// one hands its token over: each DELETE has only `deleteTimeout` of its
53	    /// own, and a cache owing three of them against a server that answers
54	    /// nothing made a person wait out fifteen seconds of a Stop they had
55	    /// already pressed (the reader review, §10.13 R1·2). What is left
56	    /// unvisited is in NEITHER list — nothing was attempted for it — which is
57	    /// safe because the one caller throws `cancelled` on the next line. The
58	    /// one IN FLIGHT is bounded rather than cut: its DELETE reads the token
59	    /// as a Stop and ends `deleteAfterStop` after it, a cut one `failed` and
60	    /// so owed like any other — kept in its file and in `janitorFailed`
61	    /// (R6-19).
62	    func retryDeletes(cancel: Transcriber.CancelToken? = nil) -> (
63	        deleted: [UInt32], failed: [UInt32]
64	    ) {
65	        guard let client else { return ([], []) }
66	        var deleted: [UInt32] = []
67	        var failed: [UInt32] = []
68	        for row in MediaTranscript.undeleted(in: cacheDirectory) {
69	            if cancel?.isCancelled == true { break }
70	            switch client.delete(id: row.transcriptID, cancel: cancel) {
71	            case .failed:
72	                failed.append(row.media)
73	                continue
74	            // An id no request could be made from is in NEITHER list: saying
75	            // `deleted` would report a delete nothing sent and would write
76	            // `remote_deleted: true` over the one record that something is
77	            // owed, and saying `failed` would HOLD the media for ever over a
78	            // string (the reader review's fix pass, §10.13).
79	            case .notSent:
80	                continue
81	            case .deleted:
82	                break
83	            }
84	            if var file = MediaTranscript.read(for: row.media, in: cacheDirectory) {
85	                file.header.remoteDeleted = true
86	                MediaTranscript.write(file, for: row.media, in: cacheDirectory)
87	            }
88	            deleted.append(row.media)
89	        }
90	        return (deleted, failed)
91	    }

93	    // MARK: - One media's round trip
94	
95	    /// Extract, upload, submit, poll, write, delete — §5a step 3 in that
96	    /// order, and the order is the whole of this method's argument.
97	    ///
98	    /// **The ten-hour refusal is first**, off the media's own `duration`,
99	    /// before a single frame is extracted: an hour of FLAC is about 55 MB and
100	    /// ten hours is 550, and finding out after sending them that AssemblyAI
101	    /// will not take the file is the most expensive possible way to learn it.
102	    ///
103	    /// **The temporary audio is removed in a `defer`**, which covers every
104	    /// exit this method has — the throw from `upload`, the throw from
105	    /// `submit`, the poll that timed out, the cancel — because an extract is
106	    /// an input to one upload and a run that failed must leave nothing in
107	    /// `NSTemporaryDirectory()` behind it. `cloud_captions_probe.py`'s row T
108	    /// globs for `framejob-upload-*` during and after a failed run rather than
109	    /// taking this comment's word for it.
110	    ///
111	    /// **The cache file is written BEFORE its marker, and the marker only
112	    /// when the file LANDED.** Either order can be interrupted; this one
113	    /// fails safe. A file with no marker is re-fetched next run (`isCurrent`
114	    /// needs both); a marker with no file would certify a transcript that is
115	    /// not there, and a marker over an OLDER file — which is what discarding
116	    /// `write`'s answer produced — certifies one that is there and is not the
117	    /// one that was asked for (the reader review, §10.13 R1·3).
118	    ///
119	    /// **The DELETE is last and its answer is recorded**, not assumed
120	    /// (R6-4). `poll` already deletes on every throwing exit of its own, so
121	    /// the only transcript this method can leave behind is one it fetched
122	    /// successfully and then failed to delete — which is what the janitor
123	    /// above is for, and what `remote_deleted: false` in the file means.
124	    func fetch(
125	        media: MediaSnapshot, url: URL, stamp: TranscriptStamp, options: TranscriptOptions,
126	        cancel: Transcriber.CancelToken,
127	        progress: @escaping (CloudProgress.Phase, Double, String) -> Void
128	    ) throws -> (file: MediaTranscript.File, uploaded: Report.Uploaded) {
129	        guard let client else { throw AccessError.credentialRequired }
130	        let name = media.name
131	        let seconds = ReelTime.seconds(media.duration)
132	        guard seconds <= Double(AssemblyAIClient.maxMediaSeconds) else {
133	            throw MediaError.tooLong(name)
134	        }
135	
136	        // 16 kHz mono is what `Transcriber+Extract.swift` writes, so the
137	        // frames a whole track will produce are its seconds times the rate —
138	        // the denominator the extract's progress is measured against.
139	        let expected = max(1, seconds * 16000)
140	        progress(.extracting, 0, CloudProgress.detail(.extracting, file: name))
141	        let upload = try Transcriber.extractUpload(
142	            url: url, name: name, cancel: cancel,
143	            progress: { frames in
144	                progress(
145	                    .extracting, Double(frames) / expected,
146	                    CloudProgress.detail(.extracting, file: name))
147	            })
148	        defer { try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: upload.url) }
149	
150	        let bytes = Int64(
151	            (try? FileManager.default.attributesOfItem(atPath: upload.url.path))?[.size]
152	                .flatMap { ($0 as? NSNumber)?.int64Value } ?? 0)
153	        progress(.uploading, 0, CloudProgress.detail(.uploading, file: name, sent: 0, total: bytes))
154	        let audioURL = try client.upload(
155	            file: upload.url, cancel: cancel,
156	            progress: { sent, total in
157	                let whole = total > 0 ? total : bytes
158	                progress(
159	                    .uploading, whole > 0 ? Double(sent) / Double(whole) : 0,
160	                    CloudProgress.detail(.uploading, file: name, sent: sent, total: whole))
161	            })
162	
163	        progress(.submitting, 0, CloudProgress.detail(.submitting, file: name))
164	        let id = try client.submit(TranscriptRequest(audioURL: audioURL, options: options))
165	        progress(.waiting, 0, CloudProgress.detail(.waiting, file: name, waited: 0))
166	        let fetched = try client.poll(
167	            id: id, audioSeconds: upload.seconds, cancel: cancel,
168	            waited: { waited in
169	                progress(
170	                    .waiting, CloudProgress.waiting(waited: waited, audioSeconds: upload.seconds),
171	                    CloudProgress.detail(.waiting, file: name, waited: waited))
172	            })
173	
174	        progress(.saving, 0, CloudProgress.detail(.saving, file: name))
175	        // The SERVER's two strings, filtered once: each goes into the cache
176	        // header, the report, the MCP `note` and the report card, and a
177	        // server that echoes the key would put it in all four (#187, R2·1).
178	        // Then bounded, and in that order, so a cut never splits the key
179	        // into a piece the filter no longer recognises (#200).
180	        let model = fetched.response.speechModelUsed.map(client.withoutCredential).map(Self.bounded)
181	        let language = fetched.response.languageCode.map(client.withoutCredential).map(Self.bounded)
182	        let header = MediaTranscript.Header(
183	            provider: MediaTranscript.provider, transcriptID: fetched.response.id,
184	            requested: options, speechModelUsed: model,
185	            languageCode: language,
186	            languageConfidence: fetched.response.languageConfidence,
187	            // Floored at 0: a negative duration is no bill (#187, item 3).
188	            audioDuration: max(
189	                0, fetched.response.audioDuration ?? Int(upload.seconds.rounded(.up))),
190	            extractedSeconds: upload.seconds, uploadedFormat: upload.format.rawValue,
191	            // ALWAYS 0 — C0's q4 measured that an extract keeps a late audio
192	            // track's head, so a word's millisecond in the extract is its
193	            // millisecond in the media (`MediaTranscript.Header`'s own doc).
194	            audioTrackStartMs: 0, fetchedAt: Self.timestamp(), remoteDeleted: false)
195	        var file = try MediaTranscript.File(header: header, wordsJSON: fetched.wordsJSON)
196	        // R6-3 keeps the served words VERBATIM, so words that repeat the key
197	        // cannot be rewritten: they are refused, and the transcript deleted,
198	        // before a byte is written (#187, R2·1). Every string literal of the
199	        // served bytes is read too, decoded — every key and value at any
200	        // depth, every value of a repeated key, read or not by
201	        // `TranscriptWord` — because an escaped key is not the key's bytes
202	        // (#200, R6-23). `wordsBytes` already decoded these words, so a
203	        // scan that fails is a fail-safe refusal, not an expected path.
204	        guard let served = TranscriptWord.servedStrings(in: fetched.wordsJSON) else {
205	            throw client.refusing(
206	                .malformed("the transcript's words did not decode"), id: fetched.response.id,
207	                cancel: cancel)
208	        }
209	        if client.carriesCredential(String(decoding: fetched.wordsJSON, as: UTF8.self))
210	            || served.contains(where: client.carriesCredential)
211	        {
212	            throw client.refusing(
213	                .malformed("the transcript's words repeat the API key"), id: fetched.response.id,
214	                cancel: cancel)
215	        }
216	        // ONLY when the file really landed. `write` answers `false` for every
217	        // way it can fail, and discarding that answer stamped the marker over
218	        // a cache file that still held an EARLIER request's words: `isCurrent`
219	        // then read the new marker and the old file and served the stale
220	        // transcript for ever, for a request it was never made from (the
221	        // reader review, §10.13 R1·3). The comment above says the marker
222	        // comes second so it fails safe; this is what makes that true.
223	        let transcriptWritten = MediaTranscript.write(file, for: media.id, in: cacheDirectory)
224	        // Its answer is KEPT: a marker that did not land means this
225	        // transcript was not kept for reuse, and the caller says so (#187,
226	        // item 2).
227	        let stampWritten = transcriptWritten
228	            && MediaTranscript.writeStamp(stamp, for: media.id, in: cacheDirectory)
229	
230	        let deleted = client.delete(id: fetched.response.id, cancel: cancel) == .deleted
231	        // Only over a first write that LANDED. A rewrite after a failed one
232	        // replaces whatever file was there — perhaps the one record of an
233	        // older id still owed a delete — and records this delete in a file
234	        // this request never wrote (#187, item 1; R6-15).
235	        if deleted && transcriptWritten {
236	            file.header.remoteDeleted = true
237	            MediaTranscript.write(file, for: media.id, in: cacheDirectory)
238	        }
239	        return (
240	            file,
241	            Report.Uploaded(
242	                media: media.id, speechModelUsed: model,
243	                languageCode: language,
244	                languageConfidence: fetched.response.languageConfidence,
245	                audioSeconds: header.audioDuration, format: upload.format,
246	                transcriptWritten: transcriptWritten,
247	                stampWritten: stampWritten,
248	                remoteDeleted: deleted)
249	        )
250	    }
251	
252	    /// The most Unicode scalars a string the SERVER names — the model and
253	    /// the language — may keep in the report, the cache header, the MCP
254	    /// answer and the report card (#200).
255	    static let serverStringLimit = 64
256	
257	    /// At most `serverStringLimit` Unicode scalars: a longer string is its
258	    /// first 63 scalars + "…" (U+2026), cut by the one scalar cutter. Not in
259	    /// `withoutCredential`, because the relayed 4xx and `error` sentences
260	    /// take their own, longer limit (`AssemblyAIClient.relayed`, R6-23).
261	    static func bounded(_ text: String) -> String {
262	        AssemblyAIClient.bounded(text, limit: serverStringLimit)
263	    }
264	
265	    /// `fetched_at`, ISO-8601 in UTC — the one spelling of a time in the
266	    /// cache file, and a fixed one: a local-time stamp would make two
267	    /// machines' files differ over nothing.
268	    private static func timestamp() -> String {
269	        let formatter = ISO8601DateFormatter()
270	        formatter.formatOptions = [.withInternetDateTime]
271	        formatter.timeZone = TimeZone(secondsFromGMT: 0)
272	        return formatter.string(from: Date())
273	    }
274	}
