3	/// The cloud run result and its shared cleanup wording.
4	extension CloudTranscriber {
5	
6	    /// Everything a caller may want to SAY about a run that the `Outcome`
7	    /// has no room for — which media were uploaded and what AssemblyAI said
8	    /// about each, which were served from the cache, and what the janitor
9	    /// managed.
10	    ///
11	    /// It is beside the outcome rather than inside it because `Outcome` is
12	    /// the shape BOTH engines answer and the on-device one has nothing to
13	    /// put in any of these fields. The tool reads it for its result keys and
14	    /// c1-chrome's report card reads it for its lines.
15	    struct Report: Equatable {
16	
17	        /// One media this run sent to AssemblyAI, and what came back.
18	        struct Uploaded: Equatable {
19	            let media: UInt32
20	            /// R6-8: which model actually ran, so a fallback is reported.
21	            let speechModelUsed: String?
22	            let languageCode: String?
23	            /// Set when the language was DETECTED, not when it was named.
24	            let languageConfidence: Double?
25	            /// Seconds as AssemblyAI reported them — what was billed.
26	            let audioSeconds: Int
27	            let format: Transcriber.UploadFormat
28	            /// Whether this fetched transcript's initial JSON write landed.
29	            let transcriptWritten: Bool
30	            /// Whether the marker landed. Always false when
31	            /// `transcriptWritten` is: the marker only follows its file.
32	            let stampWritten: Bool
33	            /// Whether the remote transcript is confirmed gone (R6-4).
34	            let remoteDeleted: Bool
35	        }
36	
37	        var uploaded: [Uploaded] = []
38	        /// Media served from `cache/transcripts/` with no request at all.
39	        var cached: [UInt32] = []
40	        /// Media whose earlier transcript the janitor deleted this run.
41	        var janitorDeleted: [UInt32] = []
42	        /// Media whose earlier transcript the janitor could NOT delete.
43	        var janitorFailed: [UInt32] = []
44	        /// Pending remote deletes retained because a keyless run sent no requests.
45	        var janitorDeferred: [UInt32] = []
46	        /// R6-11: in `janitorFailed` AND this run would otherwise have
47	        /// fetched them. A held media is in neither `uploaded` nor `cached`
48	        /// and its clips are reported as problems: its cache file is the one
49	        /// record of an id we still have to delete, and a fetch would
50	        /// overwrite it.
51	        var held: [UInt32] = []
52	        /// Media whose transcript was refused after AssemblyAI made it and
53	        /// whose DELETE answered `failed`. No file holds its id, so it is
54	        /// owed with no retry (R6-20).
55	        var refusedUndeleted: [UInt32] = []
56	
57	        /// What was billed: every uploaded media's `audioSeconds`, the one
58	        /// reducer `AgentServer`'s bill sentence and its `audio_seconds` key
59	        /// both read.
60	        ///
61	        /// SATURATING, because every term is the SERVER's own
62	        /// `audio_duration` and `+` traps: two media answered
63	        /// `9223372036854775807` killed the whole app after both had been
64	        /// uploaded and billed (the reader review, §10.13 R1·1). Each term is
65	        /// floored at 0 first, so the sum only grows and an overflow can only
66	        /// be upward: `Int.max` is sticky, and a later negative term cannot
67	        /// pull a saturated total back down (#187, item 4).
68	        var billedSeconds: Int {
69	            uploaded.reduce(0) { sum, row in
70	                let (total, overflowed) = sum.addingReportingOverflow(max(0, row.audioSeconds))
71	                return overflowed ? Int.max : total
72	            }
73	        }
74	
75	        /// One sentence per uploaded media whose marker did not land, in
76	        /// `uploaded` order (#187, item 2).
77	        ///
78	        /// It states only what `fetch` knows and promises nothing about the
79	        /// next run: on a `refresh` run over a current cache an older file
80	        /// and marker equal to this stamp survive the failed write and are
81	        /// served next time — the rule `AgentServer.billed`'s doc records
82	        /// (issue #29).
83	        func cacheWarnings(name: (UInt32) -> String) -> [String] {
84	            uploaded.filter { !$0.stampWritten }.map {
85	                "The transcript of \(name($0.media)) could not be kept in the project for reuse."
86	            }
87	        }
88	
89	        /// Cleanup still owed, in stable per-media order. An ID can be
90	        /// retried only when its transcript JSON was saved in the project.
91	        func deletionWarnings(name: (UInt32) -> String) -> [String] {
92	            var seen: Set<UInt32> = []
93	            var warnings: [String] = []
94	            func append(_ id: UInt32, written: Bool) {
95	                guard seen.insert(id).inserted else { return }
96	                let target = name(id)
97	                var warning: String
98	                if written {
99	                    warning = "AssemblyAI has not confirmed deleting the transcript of \(target); "
100	                        + "it will be retried at the next run with an API key."
101	                } else {
102	                    warning = "AssemblyAI has not confirmed deleting the transcript of \(target). "
103	                        + "Its transcript could not be saved in the project, so Frame Job cannot "
104	                        + "retry deleting it automatically. Delete it in your AssemblyAI dashboard."
105	                }
106	                if held.contains(id) { warning += " It was not uploaded again in this run." }
107	                warnings.append(warning)
108	            }
109	            for id in janitorFailed { append(id, written: true) }
110	            for id in janitorDeferred where seen.insert(id).inserted {
111	                warnings.append(
112	                    "AssemblyAI has not confirmed deleting the transcript of \(name(id)); "
113	                        + "cleanup was deferred because no API key is set. Its deletion ID is "
114	                        + "retained in the project; a later run with a key for the originating "
115	                        + "account and region will retry deletion only if that ID is safe to send.")
116	            }
117	            for row in uploaded where !row.remoteDeleted {
118	                append(row.media, written: row.transcriptWritten)
119	            }
120	            for id in refusedUndeleted { append(id, written: false) }
121	            return warnings
122	        }
123	    }
124	
125	}

3	/// Frame Job ▸ Settings… ⌘, — road map 6 §5d's window, and the app's first
4	/// piece of chrome for something PERSISTED beyond view state.
5	///
6	/// **A window and not a sheet, deliberately.** A sheet belongs to a document
7	/// and these settings belong to the person: the key and the region are the
8	/// same whichever project is open, and the Settings item has to work with no
9	/// document open at all (`WelcomeWindowController` is what is on screen
10	/// then). `ExportQueueWindowController` is the mould — one instance for the
11	/// life of the process, `isReleasedWhenClosed = false` because the controller
12	/// owns the window, `applyBackground()` in `show()` so a window reopened
13	/// after an appearance change repaints, and no frame autosave, because this
14	/// window is one fixed lockup and remembering where it was is not worth a
15	/// key. It is NOT `isExcludedFromWindowsMenu`: unlike the queue, nothing in
16	/// the Window menu opens it, so AppKit's own row is the only way back to a
17	/// window the person has buried.
18	///
19	/// **Four panes, "MCP", "Assistant", "Transcription" then "Playback"** (issue
20	/// batch B74's `MCPSettingsPane`, spec §11 MC-7; road map 12 A2's
21	/// `AssistantSettingsPane`; `transcriptionPane`; then G-38's
22	/// `PlaybackSettingsPane`), each a vertical stack
23	/// and each one of `content`'s arranged subviews, 24 pt apart through
24	/// `content.spacing`. §5d's one pane was taken as a HEADING inside a window
25	/// titled Settings rather than as a tab bar with one tab. The Assistant,
26	/// Transcription and Playback panes open with `settingsSectionHeader` — a heading and a
27	/// `SettingsInfoButton` whose popover holds its explanation (spec §11 SH-5);
28	/// the MCP pane opens with its bare heading and shows its blurb, because
29	/// MC-7 asked for the text above its button. There is still a Transcription
30	/// section, so the sentence the `transcribe` tool and its catalog entry both
31	/// print — the one that sends a caller to Settings and then to Transcription
32	/// — stays true without either of them being edited. The window's first
33	/// responder is the Assistant key field, so the MCP pane's selectable path
34	/// never opens selected. **A later section is one more pane**: a vertical
35	/// stack, put in `buildContent`'s pane list where it belongs; the gap comes
36	/// from `content.spacing`, so nothing else moves.

3	/// AssemblyAI's REST API, as five synchronous methods — road map 6 §5c
4	/// whole. Foundation only: no AppKit, no document, nothing about a project,
5	/// so a probe drives it against the stand-in server over a socket and, for
6	/// the retry and backoff rules, against an injected `URLProtocol` with no
7	/// socket at all.
8	///
9	/// **R6-7: no `async`.** Each method builds a task and waits on a semaphore
10	/// the delegate signals — the shape the old on-device `TaskSink` had, and
11	/// the delegate queue is one of ours for its reason: the framework's default
12	/// would make an off-main tool's wait depend on somebody else's queue staying
13	/// free.
14	///
15	/// **A redirect is never followed.** `willPerformHTTPRedirection` always
16	/// answers nil, so the 3xx is delivered as the task's own response and comes
17	/// back as `.redirected`. Following one would re-send the `authorization`
18	/// header to whatever host the `Location` named — the spike's Python client
19	/// needed a `NoRedirect` handler for exactly this.
20	///
21	/// **The credential is in one header and in no log line.** A log line carries
22	/// a method, a path and a status; the session is `.ephemeral` with its
23	/// cookie, cache and credential storage cleared, so the framework writes
24	/// nothing about a request to disk either.
25	final class AssemblyAIClient {
26	
27	    /// The numbers road map 6 §8 says a person may want to change, in one
28	    /// value a probe can replace wholesale.
29	    struct Tuning: Equatable {
30	        /// Seconds between polls — AssemblyAI's own SDKs' default.
31	        var pollInterval: TimeInterval
32	        /// The poll ceiling never falls below this, however short the audio.
33	        var pollCeilingFloor: TimeInterval
34	        /// Audio seconds per second of ceiling: floor(147 ÷ 3) from C0's q8,
35	        /// which measured an hour completing in 24.4 s — three times the
36	        /// measured rate is the margin a queue can eat.
37	        var pollCeilingDivisor: Double
38	        /// One retry: a dropped socket's worth, and two uploads of a 100 MB
39	        /// file are the cost of a third.
40	        var uploadRetries: Int
41	        var retryBackoff: TimeInterval
42	        /// Consecutive 5xx or transport errors a poll loop tolerates.
43	        var pollFailuresTolerated: Int
44	        /// The janitor's budget per item; the slowest DELETE C0 timed was
45	        /// 1.70 s.
46	        var deleteTimeout: TimeInterval
47	        /// Every other request's ceiling.
48	        var requestTimeout: TimeInterval
49	        /// Looks at the newest transcript page after an ambiguous submit.
50	        var submitRecoveryAttempts: Int = 3
51	        var submitRecoveryDelay: TimeInterval = 2.5
52	        var submitRecoveryTimeout: TimeInterval = 5
53	        /// How long a DELETE runs on after a Stop, in wall clock from the
54	        /// later of the Stop and its own start (R6-19): above C0's slowest
55	        /// DELETE, so a Stop during a submit or a wait still deletes.
56	        var deleteAfterStop: TimeInterval = 2
57	
58	        static let shipped = Tuning(
59	            pollInterval: 3, pollCeilingFloor: 300, pollCeilingDivisor: 49, uploadRetries: 1,
60	            retryBackoff: 1, pollFailuresTolerated: 3, deleteTimeout: 5, requestTimeout: 60)
61	
62	        /// `max(300 s, audio seconds / 49)` — §8's row.
63	        func pollCeiling(audioSeconds: Double) -> TimeInterval {
64	            guard pollCeilingDivisor > 0 else { return pollCeilingFloor }
65	            return max(pollCeilingFloor, audioSeconds / pollCeilingDivisor)
66	        }
67	    }

70	    /// minutes of processing at q8's rate, and 550 MB of FLAC.
71	    static let maxMediaSeconds = 36_000
72	    /// `keyterms_prompt`'s documented ceiling on Universal-3.5 Pro.

172	    /// `POST /v2/upload` — the body streams from the file and is never in
173	    /// memory. One retry on a transport error or a 5xx, none on a 4xx.
174	    func upload(
175	        file: URL, cancel: Transcriber.CancelToken? = nil,
176	        progress: ((Int64, Int64) -> Void)? = nil
177	    ) throws -> URL {
178	        var request = self.request("POST", path: "/v2/upload")
179	        request.setValue("application/octet-stream", forHTTPHeaderField: "content-type")
180	        var attempt = 0
181	        while true {
182	            if cancel?.isCancelled == true { throw ClientError.cancelled }
183	            let reply = send(request, file: file, cancel: cancel, progress: progress)
184	            if let failure = classify(reply) {
185	                guard failure.isRetriable, attempt < tuning.uploadRetries,
186	                    cancel?.isCancelled != true
187	                else { throw failure }
188	                attempt += 1
189	                note("retry \(attempt) of upload after \(failure.shortName)")
190	                sleep(tuning.retryBackoff, cancel: cancel)
191	                continue
192	            }
193	            guard
194	                let object = try? JSONSerialization.jsonObject(with: reply.data)
195	                    as? [String: Any], let text = object["upload_url"] as? String,
196	                let url = URL(string: text)
197	            else { throw ClientError.malformed("the upload answered no `upload_url`") }
198	            return url
199	        }
200	    }

202	    /// `GET /v2/transcript/{id}` every `pollInterval` until it is
203	    /// `completed`, it is `error`, the ceiling passes or the token is
204	    /// cancelled.
205	    ///
206	    /// **Every throwing exit deletes the transcript first** (R6-4): one
207	    /// `delete(id:cancel:)`, best effort, before the throw. A transcript AssemblyAI
208	    /// is still making, or has made and nobody read, is one it keeps
209	    /// indefinitely, and this is the one place that knows its id.
210	    ///
211	    /// **A `completed` body with no words array is `.malformed`, never an
212	    /// empty transcript.** `[]` is an array and means zero words, a real
213	    /// answer about audio nobody spoke in; an absent `words`, a `null` one
214	    /// and an object are bodies this client cannot read, and turning one into
215	    /// "nothing was said" would cache a broken response as a fact.
216	    func poll(
217	        id: String, audioSeconds: Double, cancel: Transcriber.CancelToken? = nil,
218	        waited: ((TimeInterval) -> Void)? = nil
219	    ) throws -> Fetched {
220	        guard isSendableIdentifier(id) else {
221	            throw ClientError.malformed("AssemblyAI answered an id that is not one")
222	        }
223	        let ceiling = tuning.pollCeiling(audioSeconds: audioSeconds)
224	        let started = Date()
225	        var failures = 0
226	        while true {
227	            if cancel?.isCancelled == true { throw refusing(.cancelled, id: id, cancel: cancel) }
228	            if Date().timeIntervalSince(started) > ceiling {
229	                throw refusing(.timedOut, id: id, cancel: cancel)
230	            }
231	            let reply = send(request("GET", path: "/v2/transcript/\(id)"), cancel: cancel)
232	            if let failure = classify(reply) {
233	                guard failure.isRetriable else { throw refusing(failure, id: id, cancel: cancel) }
234	                failures += 1
235	                note("poll \(id) failed (\(failure.shortName)), \(failures) in a row")
236	                if failures > tuning.pollFailuresTolerated {
237	                    throw refusing(failure, id: id, cancel: cancel)
238	                }
239	            } else {
240	                failures = 0
241	                guard
242	                    let response = try? JSONDecoder().decode(
243	                        TranscriptResponse.self, from: reply.data)
244	                else {
245	                    throw refusing(
246	                        .malformed("the transcript did not decode"), id: id, cancel: cancel)
247	                }
248	                if response.status == "error" {
249	                    throw refusing(
250	                        .transcript(
251	                            relayed(
252	                                response.error ?? "AssemblyAI could not transcribe it")),
253	                        id: id, cancel: cancel)
254	                }
255	                if response.status == "completed" {
256	                    try requireEchoedID(response, polled: id, cancel: cancel)
257	                    guard let words = wordsBytes(in: reply.data) else {
258	                        throw refusing(
259	                            .malformed("the transcript came back completed with no words array"),
260	                            id: id, cancel: cancel)
261	                    }
262	                    return Fetched(response: response, wordsJSON: words)
263	                }
264	            }
265	            waited?(Date().timeIntervalSince(started))
266	            sleep(tuning.pollInterval, cancel: cancel)
267	        }
268	    }

270	    /// What an AssemblyAI transcript id may be, and the ONE gate both calls
271	    /// that interpolate one into a path go through.
272	    ///
273	    /// An id reaches this client from two places that are not this app: the
274	    /// `transcript_id` of a cache file, which rides inside a `.framejob`
275	    /// package and can be hand-edited or authored by somebody else, and a
276	    /// submission's own reply. `URL.appendingPathComponent` does not resolve
277	    /// `..` and `URLSession` sends the path as written, so
278	    /// `"transcript_id": "../../v1/anything"` in a package made a DELETE go
279	    /// to a path of its author's choosing on the API host, carrying the
280	    /// person's key (the reader review, road map 6 §10.13, R3·1). Letters,
281	    /// digits, `-` and `_` are what the service's own ids are made of, and a
282	    /// bounded length is what keeps a megabyte of them off the wire.
283	    static func isPlainIdentifier(_ id: String) -> Bool {
284	        guard !id.isEmpty, id.count <= 128 else { return false }
285	        return id.allSatisfy { $0.isASCII && ($0.isLetter || $0.isNumber || $0 == "-" || $0 == "_") }
286	    }
287	
288	    /// What one DELETE answered. THREE states, because "never sent" is
289	    /// neither "gone" nor "owed" (the reader review's fix pass, §10.13).
290	    enum DeleteAnswer { case deleted, failed, notSent }
291	
292	    /// `DELETE /v2/transcript/{id}` on `deleteTimeout`. Best effort by
293	    /// design: a `failed` delete is RECORDED in the cache file and retried by
294	    /// the next run's janitor, and a repeat answers 200 (q6), so a retry
295	    /// cannot make things worse.
296	    ///
297	    /// **An id that is not one is `notSent`, with no request at all.**
298	    /// AssemblyAI cannot have minted it, so there is nothing to delete;
299	    /// `failed` would put the media in `janitorFailed` and R6-11 would HOLD
300	    /// it for ever over a string, and `deleted` would report — and write into
301	    /// the cache file — a delete this app never asked for.
302	    ///
303	    /// **`cancel` is read as a STOP and never attached** (R6-19). Attaching
304	    /// would cancel the DELETE at the press, orphaning the transcript of
305	    /// every Stop during a submit or a wait; instead the DELETE is cut
306	    /// `deleteAfterStop` of wall clock after the later of the Stop and its
307	    /// own start, and a cut one is `failed` — owed, as any failed one is. No
308	    /// default: every caller names the token it has, or nil.
309	    @discardableResult
310	    func delete(id: String, cancel: Transcriber.CancelToken?) -> DeleteAnswer {
311	        guard isSendableIdentifier(id) else {
312	            note("refusing to DELETE an id that is not one")
313	            return .notSent
314	        }
315	        var request = self.request("DELETE", path: "/v2/transcript/\(id)")
316	        request.timeoutInterval = tuning.deleteTimeout
317	        let reply = send(request, stop: cancel, grace: tuning.deleteAfterStop)
318	        return classify(reply) == nil ? .deleted : .failed
319	    }
320	
321	    // MARK: - One request
322	
323	    /// `request` and `send` stay in this file and not in `+Session.swift`
324	    /// because they are two of the THREE members that touch `credential`,
325	    /// `delegate` and `session`, which are `private` — and `private` on a
326	    /// stored property does not cross a file. Keeping them here is what lets
327	    /// the credential stay private rather than being widened for a size toll.
328	    /// The third is `withoutCredential(_:)` above, which the reader review
329	    /// added for the same reason and in the same place (§10.13, R2·1).
330	    func request(_ method: String, path: String, query: String? = nil) -> URLRequest {
331	        var components = URLComponents(
332	            url: base.appendingPathComponent(path), resolvingAgainstBaseURL: false)
333	        components?.query = query
334	        var request = URLRequest(url: components?.url ?? base.appendingPathComponent(path))
335	        request.httpMethod = method
336	        request.setValue(credential, forHTTPHeaderField: "authorization")
337	        request.timeoutInterval = tuning.requestTimeout
338	        return request
339	    }
340	
341	    /// Builds the task, hands the delegate its sink, waits. The wait has no
342	    /// deadline of its own but a Stop's: `timeoutIntervalForRequest` is the
343	    /// idle bound, and a second one here would leave a task running with
344	    /// nobody to read it. A token is read one of two ways: `cancel` is
345	    /// ATTACHED, so a Stop cancels the task at the press; `stop` never is —
346	    /// `waitForReply` cuts the task `grace` seconds after it is first seen
347	    /// set and still waits for its completion. Only `delete` passes a `stop`
348	    /// (R6-19).
349	    func send(
350	        _ request: URLRequest, file: URL? = nil, cancel: Transcriber.CancelToken? = nil,
351	        stop: Transcriber.CancelToken? = nil, grace: TimeInterval = 0,
352	        progress: ((Int64, Int64) -> Void)? = nil
353	    ) -> Reply {
354	        let task =
355	            file.map { session.uploadTask(with: request, fromFile: $0) }
356	            ?? session.dataTask(with: request)
357	        let sink = delegate.open(task.taskIdentifier, progress: progress)
358	        cancel?.attach(task)
359	        task.resume()
360	        waitForReply(sink.done, task: task, stop: stop, grace: grace)
361	        cancel?.release()
362	        let reply = delegate.close(task.taskIdentifier)
363	        note("\(request.httpMethod ?? "?") \(request.url?.path ?? "?") → "
364	            + "\(reply.response?.statusCode.description ?? reply.error.map { _ in "error" } ?? "?")")
365	        return reply
366	    }
367	
368	    /// A sentence the SERVER wrote, with this client's own credential taken
369	    /// out of it.
370	    ///
371	    /// Three sentences are relayed as the service wrote them — a 402's, a
372	    /// 4xx's and a transcript's `error` — as AssemblyAI says the useful thing
373	    /// (R6-6); `relayed` (`+Session`) filters each here, then bounds it
374	    /// (R6-23). But that text is somebody ELSE's, and a server echoing the
375	    /// `authorization` header it received puts the key in it: a stand-in
376	    /// answering `400 … for <the key>` put the credential straight into an
377	    /// MCP refusal, which `AgentServer+CloudCaptions.swift`'s header promises
378	    /// never happens (the reader review, road map 6 §10.13, R2·1). This is
379	    /// the one place that can know the string to look for, because
380	    /// `credential` is `private` and does not cross a file.
381	    func withoutCredential(_ text: String) -> String {
382	        guard !credential.isEmpty, text.contains(credential) else { return text }
383	        return text.replacingOccurrences(of: credential, with: "<redacted>")
384	    }
385	
386	    /// `GET /v2/transcript?limit=1` — the cheapest authenticated call, for
387	    /// the Settings window's Verify button.
388	    func verify() -> Result<Void, ClientError> {
389	        let reply = send(request("GET", path: "/v2/transcript", query: "limit=1"))
390	        if let failure = classify(reply) { return .failure(failure) }
391	        return .success(())
392	    }
393	}

5	/// What a reply MEANS and who delivers it: `Reply`, the status classifier,
6	/// the two readers that cut a served body apart, the one-delete-then-throw
7	/// helper and the `Refusal` it answers (R6-20), the cancellable wait, the
8	/// wait for a reply that a Stop bounds (`waitForReply`, R6-19), the log
9	/// line — and `SessionDelegate`, the object `URLSession` calls back on its
10	/// own one-wide queue. At the foot,
11	/// `ClientError`'s two readings, `isRetriable` and `shortName`: a pure move
12	/// out of `AssemblyAIClient.swift`, which stood at 399 lines against the
13	/// cap when a DELETE learned to read a Stop (issue batch B35).
14	///
15	/// It is beside `AssemblyAIClient.swift` rather than in it because that file
16	/// holds road map 6 §5c's five calls and §8's numbers and stood at 487 lines
17	/// with this in it, against the 400-line cap on a new file (app/CLAUDE.md,
18	/// road map 6 §5h). The split is the one the spec already made for
19	/// `AssemblyAITranscript.swift`, one seam further along: the wire VALUES
20	/// left first, then the wire MACHINERY, so what is left in the client file
21	/// is the five calls a reader came for.
22	///
23	/// `request` and `send` did NOT come here, and neither did
24	/// `withoutCredential(_:)`. Those three are the members that touch
25	/// `credential`, `delegate` and `session`, and `private` on a stored property
26	/// does not cross a file: moving them would have widened the credential to
27	/// pay a size toll, which is the wrong direction. `classify` below CALLS
28	/// `withoutCredential` and does not name the credential itself.
29	extension AssemblyAIClient {
30	
31	    struct Reply {
32	        var data = Data()
33	        var response: HTTPURLResponse?
34	        var error: (any Error)?
35	    }
36	
37	    /// The status a reply carries, as an error or nil. A redirect arrives
38	    /// as a 3xx because the delegate refused to follow it.
39	    func classify(_ reply: Reply) -> ClientError? {
40	        if let error = reply.error as? URLError {
41	            switch error.code {
42	            case .cancelled: return .cancelled
43	            case .timedOut: return .timedOut
44	            default: return .noNetwork
45	            }
46	        }
47	        if reply.error != nil { return .noNetwork }
48	        guard let response = reply.response else {
49	            return .malformed("the request answered nothing at all")
50	        }
51	        let code = response.statusCode
52	        switch code {
53	        case 200..<300: return nil
54	        case 300..<400: return .redirected(code)
55	        case 401, 403: return .keyRefused(code)
56	        case 402:
57	            return .account(
58	                relayed(sentence(in: reply.data) ?? "AssemblyAI answered \(code)"))
59	        case 400..<500:
60	            return .request(
61	                relayed(sentence(in: reply.data) ?? "AssemblyAI answered \(code)"))
62	        default: return .server(code)
63	        }
64	    }
65	
66	    /// AssemblyAI's own `error` sentence out of a body, relayed as the
67	    /// service wrote it — through `relayed`, which takes this client's key
68	    /// out and then bounds it (R6-23), so the promise is about the SERVER's
69	    /// words and not about this client's key or an endless body.
70	    private func sentence(in data: Data) -> String? {
71	        guard let object = try? JSONSerialization.jsonObject(with: data) as? [String: Any],
72	            let text = object["error"] as? String, !text.isEmpty
73	        else { return nil }
74	        return text
75	    }
76	
77	    /// The most Unicode scalars a sentence the SERVER wrote — a 402's, a
78	    /// 4xx's, a transcript's `error` — keeps where the app relays it
79	    /// (R6-23). A ceiling against a broken or hostile server, not a measured
80	    /// length.
81	    static let relayedSentenceLimit = 300
82	
83	    /// At most `limit` Unicode scalars: a longer string is its first
84	    /// `limit - 1` scalars + "…" (U+2026). The one scalar cutter — the
85	    /// relayed sentences here, and `CloudTranscriber.bounded`'s model and
86	    /// language (R6-23).
87	    static func bounded(_ text: String, limit: Int) -> String {
88	        let scalars = text.unicodeScalars
89	        guard scalars.count > limit else { return text }
90	        var kept = String.UnicodeScalarView(scalars.prefix(limit - 1))
91	        kept.append("\u{2026}")
92	        return String(kept)
93	    }
94	
95	    /// A sentence the server wrote, as the app relays it: the key filtered
96	    /// out FIRST, then cut, so a cut never splits the key into a piece the
97	    /// filter cannot see (R6-23).
98	    func relayed(_ text: String) -> String {
99	        Self.bounded(withoutCredential(text), limit: Self.relayedSentenceLimit)
100	    }
101	
102	    /// The served bytes of a top-level `words` ARRAY, or nil when the key is
103	    /// absent, does not begin `[`, or will not decode as words.
104	    func wordsBytes(in body: Data) -> Data? {
105	        guard let range = JSONValueRange.topLevel(key: "words", in: body) else { return nil }
106	        let bytes = body.subdata(in: range)
107	        guard bytes.first == UInt8(ascii: "[") else { return nil }
108	        guard (try? JSONDecoder().decode([TranscriptWord].self, from: bytes)) != nil else {
109	            return nil
110	        }
111	        return bytes
112	    }
113	
114	    /// Whether `text` repeats this client's own credential — the question
115	    /// `withoutCredential` answers by changing the text, asked without it.
116	    func carriesCredential(_ text: String) -> Bool {
117	        withoutCredential(text) != text
118	    }
119	
120	    /// The ONE gate for a transcript id this client puts in a path (`poll`,
121	    /// `delete`) or accepts from a submit reply or a recovery-list row: plain
122	    /// (`isPlainIdentifier`) AND not the credential. An id that repeats the
123	    /// key would put it in a request path and a log line, so it is never
124	    /// sent and never accepted (#187, R2·1).
125	    func isSendableIdentifier(_ id: String) -> Bool {
126	        Self.isPlainIdentifier(id) && !carriesCredential(id)
127	    }
128	
129	    /// A transcript refused after AssemblyAI made it, and what refusing's
130	    /// DELETE of it answered (#201, R6-20). It reads as `failure`'s own
131	    /// sentence; `CloudTranscriber.transcribe` records a `failed` deletion
132	    /// in `Report.refusedUndeleted` and then reads `failure` alone.
133	    struct Refusal: LocalizedError, Equatable {
134	        let failure: ClientError
135	        let deletion: DeleteAnswer
136	
137	        var errorDescription: String? { failure.errorDescription }
138	    }
139	
140	    /// One `delete` before a throw, and the error to throw, carrying that
141	    /// delete's answer.
142	    func refusing(
143	        _ failure: ClientError, id: String, cancel: Transcriber.CancelToken?
144	    ) -> Refusal {
145	        Refusal(failure: failure, deletion: delete(id: id, cancel: cancel))
146	    }
147	
148	    /// A `completed` body must name the id that was polled, or it is
149	    /// `.malformed` (#71).
150	    ///
151	    /// `fetch` stores `response.id` in the cache file and later deletes it,
152	    /// so a body served under another id — `../upload`, or a plain id that
153	    /// is somebody else's — would be cached and promised a retry that can
154	    /// never be sent, or would move the DELETE to a transcript this run
155	    /// never made. Refusing here keeps the id `fetch` stores and deletes the
156	    /// submitted one, and `refusing` deletes the POLLED id, which is plain.
157	    func requireEchoedID(
158	        _ response: TranscriptResponse, polled id: String, cancel: Transcriber.CancelToken?
159	    ) throws {
160	        guard response.id != id else { return }
161	        throw refusing(
162	            .malformed(
163	                "the transcript came back completed under an id other than the one polled"),
164	            id: id, cancel: cancel)
165	    }
166	
167	    /// Waits in slices of at most a tenth of a second, reading the token
168	    /// between them, so a cancel during a three-second gap is acted on in a
169	    /// tenth rather than at the next poll.
170	    func sleep(_ seconds: TimeInterval, cancel: Transcriber.CancelToken?) {
171	        var left = seconds
172	        while left > 0 {
173	            if cancel?.isCancelled == true { return }
174	            let slice = min(0.1, left)
175	            Thread.sleep(forTimeInterval: slice)
176	            left -= slice
177	        }
178	    }
179	
180	    /// Waits for `done`, and with a `stop` token bounds the wait (R6-19).
181	    /// The token is read at the start and after every slice of at most a
182	    /// tenth of a second; once `grace` seconds of wall clock have passed
183	    /// since the first reading that saw it set, the task is cancelled and
184	    /// its completion — which a cancel always delivers — is waited for, so
185	    /// no task is left running with nobody to read it. Wall clock, because a
186	    /// server that drips resets the idle timeout on every byte (R6-18). No
187	    /// `stop` is `done.wait()`, exactly as before. No queue, timer or
188	    /// thread: `sleep(_:cancel:)`'s slices, on the calling thread.
189	    func waitForReply(
190	        _ done: DispatchSemaphore, task: URLSessionTask, stop: Transcriber.CancelToken?,
191	        grace: TimeInterval
192	    ) {
193	        guard let stop else {
194	            done.wait()
195	            return
196	        }
197	        var stoppedAt: Date? = stop.isCancelled ? Date() : nil
198	        while true {
199	            if let stoppedAt, Date().timeIntervalSince(stoppedAt) >= grace {
200	                task.cancel()
201	                done.wait()
202	                return
203	            }
204	            if done.wait(timeout: .now() + 0.1) == .success { return }
205	            if stoppedAt == nil, stop.isCancelled { stoppedAt = Date() }
206	        }
207	    }
208	
209	    /// A method, a path and a status. Never a header and never a body:
210	    /// `authorization` is in one, a signed URL may be in the other. Named
211	    /// `note` rather than `log` because Darwin's `log(_:)` is a global
212	    /// function on `Double` and an unqualified `log("…")` resolves to it.
213	    ///
214	    /// Written straight to fd 1 through `FileHandle.standardOutput`, never
215	    /// `print` (#116): `print` is block-buffered (4096 B) under a file
216	    /// redirect, so an instance log held only the lines before the last full
217	    /// block. The throwing `write(contentsOf:)` because the legacy
218	    /// `write(_:)` raises an Objective-C exception on a bad descriptor.
219	    func note(_ line: String) {
220	        try? FileHandle.standardOutput.write(contentsOf: Data("AssemblyAI: \(line)\n".utf8))
221	    }

223	    // MARK: - The delegate
224	
225	    /// One object for the whole session, holding a sink per task under a
226	    /// lock: the delegate queue is not the calling thread and a method here
227	    /// can arrive while another task is being opened.
228	    final class SessionDelegate: NSObject, URLSessionDataDelegate {
229	        final class Sink {
230	            let done = DispatchSemaphore(value: 0)
231	            var reply = Reply()
232	            var progress: ((Int64, Int64) -> Void)?
233	            var signalled = false
234	        }
235	
236	        private let lock = NSLock()
237	        private var sinks: [Int: Sink] = [:]
238	
239	        func open(_ identifier: Int, progress: ((Int64, Int64) -> Void)?) -> Sink {
240	            let sink = Sink()
241	            sink.progress = progress
242	            lock.lock()
243	            sinks[identifier] = sink
244	            lock.unlock()
245	            return sink
246	        }
247	
248	        func close(_ identifier: Int) -> Reply {
249	            lock.lock()
250	            let sink = sinks.removeValue(forKey: identifier)
251	            lock.unlock()
252	            return sink?.reply ?? Reply()
253	        }
254	
255	        private func sink(_ identifier: Int) -> Sink? {
256	            lock.lock()
257	            defer { lock.unlock() }
258	            return sinks[identifier]
259	        }
260	
261	        func urlSession(_ session: URLSession, dataTask: URLSessionDataTask, didReceive data: Data)
262	        {
263	            guard let sink = sink(dataTask.taskIdentifier) else { return }
264	            lock.lock()
265	            sink.reply.data.append(data)
266	            lock.unlock()
267	        }
268	
269	        func urlSession(
270	            _ session: URLSession, task: URLSessionTask, didCompleteWithError error: (any Error)?
271	        ) {
272	            guard let sink = sink(task.taskIdentifier) else { return }
273	            lock.lock()
274	            sink.reply.response = task.response as? HTTPURLResponse
275	            sink.reply.error = error
276	            let already = sink.signalled
277	            sink.signalled = true
278	            lock.unlock()
279	            if !already { sink.done.signal() }
280	        }
281	
282	        func urlSession(
283	            _ session: URLSession, task: URLSessionTask, didSendBodyData bytesSent: Int64,
284	            totalBytesSent: Int64, totalBytesExpectedToSend: Int64
285	        ) {
286	            sink(task.taskIdentifier)?.progress?(totalBytesSent, totalBytesExpectedToSend)
287	        }
288	
289	        /// Never followed. Answering nil delivers the 3xx as the task's own
290	        /// response, which `classify` turns into `.redirected`: the
291	        /// `authorization` header goes to no host but its own.
292	        func urlSession(
293	            _ session: URLSession, task: URLSessionTask,
294	            willPerformHTTPRedirection response: HTTPURLResponse, newRequest request: URLRequest,
295	            completionHandler: @escaping (URLRequest?) -> Void
296	        ) {
297	            completionHandler(nil)
298	        }
299	    }
300	}

150	        _ = installed
151	        guard let item else { return enabled }

169	    /// else changes, and no suffix is ever added here.

171	        guard let menu else { return }
172	        var actions: Set<Selector> = []

3	/// Where the person's AssemblyAI key lives, behind a protocol with three
4	/// verbs — and the two conformers this build ships: a `0600` file, and a
5	/// value in memory that never touches disk.
6	///
7	/// **Why a file and not the Keychain.** The Keychain is the better place and
8	/// was the plan. Road map 6 §3 q7 MEASURED what an ad-hoc signature does to a
9	/// login-keychain item: the next build blocks on a `SecurityAgent` modal for
10	/// a full twenty seconds — even with `kSecUseAuthenticationUIFail`, which
11	/// does not turn that ACL confirmation into a refusal — and its delete
12	/// answers `errSecInvalidOwnerEdit`, so the item cannot even be cleaned up by
13	/// the build that finds it. Every `make app` is a new ad-hoc signature, and
14	/// an agent-driven instance has nobody to click the modal. The
15	/// data-protection keychain is not a way out either: `SecItemAdd` there
16	/// answered `errSecMissingEntitlement` from an unsandboxed ad-hoc-signed app
17	/// with no keychain access group. **The file is the weaker choice and this
18	/// paragraph is the record of it**: it is readable by anything running as the
19	/// person, where a Keychain item is readable by one signed identity after one
20	/// confirmation. The protocol is what lets a build signed with a stable
21	/// Developer ID identity add a `KeychainStore` conformer and a one-time
22	/// migration later without touching anything above it (R6-5, road map 6 §5d).
23	///
24	/// **No proof ever reads the person's file.** `MemoryStore` is what a probe
25	/// gets, and R6-9's `-RCSecretFolder` is what moves a launched app's folder
26	/// somewhere disposable — `AssemblyAIConfiguration.store` is the one place
27	/// either is decided.
28	protocol SecretStore {
29	    /// The secret, or nil when there is none. Never throws: "no key set" is a
30	    /// state the sheet names, not an error (road map 6 §5d).
31	    func read() -> String?
32	    /// Replaces whatever is there. Throws when it cannot be written, because
33	    /// a Save button that said nothing and saved nothing is the failure this
34	    /// is for.
35	    func write(_ secret: String) throws
36	    /// Leaves nothing behind. Removing what is not there succeeds.
37	    func remove() throws
38	}
39	
40	/// Why a store could not be written, in a sentence the Settings window can
41	/// show unchanged.
42	enum SecretStoreError: LocalizedError, Equatable {
43	    case unwritable(String)
44	
45	    var errorDescription: String? {
46	        switch self {
47	        case .unwritable(let reason):
48	            return "The API key could not be saved: \(reason)"
49	        }
50	    }
51	}
52	
53	/// The shipping conformer: one file, mode `0600`, in a directory created at
54	/// `0700`.
55	///
56	/// **The permissions are on the file from the moment it exists.** It is
57	/// created with `O_CREAT|O_EXCL` at mode `0600` under a temporary name and
58	/// `rename(2)`d into place — never written first and `chmod`ed after, which
59	/// would leave a window in which the key was world-readable, and never
60	/// through `Data.write`, whose `POSIXPermissions` would be applied to a file
61	/// that already existed. The rename is also what makes a replacement atomic:
62	/// a reader sees the old key or the new one, never a half-written file.
63	///
64	/// An EXISTING directory's mode is left alone. A person who tightened
65	/// `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/` themselves should keep what they
66	/// chose, and a directory the app did not create is not the app's to relax.
67	final class FileStore: SecretStore {
68	
69	    /// The one spelling of AssemblyAI's file's name, and `name`'s default.
70	    static let fileName = "assemblyai-key"
71	
72	    /// The folder the file sits in. `AssemblyAIConfiguration.store` and
73	    /// `AssistantConfiguration.store` resolve it — from `AppSupport.directory`
74	    /// for a person, from `-RCSecretFolder` for a proof — and nothing here
75	    /// reaches for a default of its own, so each key has exactly one line in
76	    /// the tree that can name a person's real folder (R6-9, AI-13).
77	    let directory: URL
78	
79	    /// The file's name in `directory`: `fileName` for AssemblyAI's key,
80	    /// `AssistantConfiguration.keyFileName` (`anthropic-key`, spec §11 AI-8,
81	    /// AI-13) for the assistant's. Each store is one file; the temporary a
82	    /// write renames into place carries the same name.
83	    let name: String
84	
85	    var fileURL: URL { directory.appendingPathComponent(name, isDirectory: false) }
86	
87	    init(directory: URL, name: String = FileStore.fileName) {
88	        self.directory = directory
89	        self.name = name
90	    }
91	
92	    /// The key, trimmed. An empty or whitespace-only file reads as NO key
93	    /// rather than as a key that is the empty string: a request with an empty
94	    /// `authorization` header would be refused by the service with the key
95	    /// sentence, and "no key is set" is the answer the person can act on.
96	    func read() -> String? {
97	        guard let data = try? Data(contentsOf: fileURL),
98	            let text = String(data: data, encoding: .utf8)
99	        else { return nil }
100	        let trimmed = text.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
101	        return trimmed.isEmpty ? nil : trimmed
102	    }
103	
104	    func write(_ secret: String) throws {
105	        try makeDirectory()
106	        let temporary = directory.appendingPathComponent(
107	            ".\(name).\(UUID().uuidString)", isDirectory: false)
108	        let descriptor = temporary.withUnsafeFileSystemRepresentation { path -> Int32 in
109	            guard let path = path else { return -1 }
110	            return open(path, O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_EXCL, 0o600)
111	        }
112	        guard descriptor >= 0 else {
113	            throw SecretStoreError.unwritable(String(cString: strerror(errno)))
114	        }
115	        if let reason = writeAll(descriptor, Array(secret.utf8)) {
116	            close(descriptor)
117	            try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: temporary)
118	            throw SecretStoreError.unwritable(reason)
119	        }
120	        close(descriptor)
121	        let moved = temporary.withUnsafeFileSystemRepresentation { from -> Int32 in
122	            guard let from = from else { return -1 }
123	            return fileURL.withUnsafeFileSystemRepresentation { to -> Int32 in
124	                guard let to = to else { return -1 }
125	                return rename(from, to)
126	            }
127	        }
128	        guard moved == 0 else {
129	            let reason = String(cString: strerror(errno))
130	            try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: temporary)
131	            throw SecretStoreError.unwritable(reason)
132	        }
133	    }
134	
135	    func remove() throws {
136	        guard FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: fileURL.path) else { return }
137	        do {
138	            try FileManager.default.removeItem(at: fileURL)
139	        } catch {
140	            throw SecretStoreError.unwritable(error.localizedDescription)
141	        }
142	    }
143	
144	    /// The directory through `AppSupport.ensureDirectory` (#108): `mkdir(2)`
145	    /// at `0700` for each level that is absent, the intermediates included,
146	    /// and nothing at all for a level that is there. One mode, never
147	    /// `chmod`ed after.
148	    private func makeDirectory() throws {
149	        do {
150	            try AppSupport.ensureDirectory(directory)
151	        } catch {
152	            throw SecretStoreError.unwritable(error.localizedDescription)
153	        }
154	    }
155	}
156	
157	/// Every byte of `bytes` to `descriptor`, or `strerror`'s sentence. A free
158	/// function because `write(2)` and `SecretStore.write(_:)` are the same name
159	/// and a method cannot call the system call without a module qualifier that
160	/// changes with the SDK.
161	///
162	/// **`EINTR` is retried and NOTHING else is.** A signal that landed while the
163	/// write was in progress is not a failure to write, and turning one into
164	/// `unwritable` loses a key the person had just typed and told them the disk
165	/// refused it (the reader review, road map 6 §10.13, H·3). Every other errno
166	/// is still the sentence it was.
167	///
168	/// **The retry is bounded**: at most `writeAllRetryLimit` interruptions per
169	/// call, and the next one answers `strerror(EINTR)`, so a writer that is
170	/// interrupted for ever cannot hold the caller for ever (#187, item 6).
171	///
172	/// **A write of 0 bytes is its own sentence**, at once and with no retry:
173	/// `write(2)` sets no `errno` when it answers 0, so `strerror(errno)` would
174	/// report whatever an earlier call left there (#187, item 6).
175	///
176	/// `using` is the probe's seam and nothing else: its default IS `write(2)`,
177	/// so the shipped path has one spelling, and a row can hand it a writer that
178	/// answers `EINTR` once before the real one runs.
179	func writeAll(
180	    _ descriptor: Int32, _ bytes: [UInt8],
181	    using write: (Int32, UnsafeRawPointer?, Int) -> Int = { Darwin.write($0, $1, $2) }
182	) -> String? {
183	    var offset = 0
184	    var interruptions = 0
185	    while offset < bytes.count {
186	        let written = bytes.withUnsafeBytes { buffer -> Int in
187	            guard let base = buffer.baseAddress else { return -1 }
188	            return write(descriptor, base + offset, buffer.count - offset)
189	        }
190	        if written > 0 {
191	            offset += written
192	            continue
193	        }
194	        if written == 0 { return "no bytes were written" }
195	        if errno == EINTR, interruptions < writeAllRetryLimit {
196	            interruptions += 1
197	            continue
198	        }
199	        return String(cString: strerror(errno))
200	    }
201	    return nil
202	}
203	
204	/// How many `EINTR`s one `writeAll` call retries before it answers one.
205	let writeAllRetryLimit = 100
206	
207	/// The probe's store, and the empty store R6-9 hands an app that was pointed
208	/// at a stand-in server. Nothing here touches disk, so no run of any
209	/// instrument can read or write the person's own key.
210	final class MemoryStore: SecretStore {
211	    private let lock = NSLock()
212	    private var secret: String?
213	
214	    init(_ secret: String? = nil) {
215	        self.secret = REDACTED
216	    }
217	
218	    func read() -> String? {
219	        lock.lock()
220	        defer { lock.unlock() }
221	        return secret
222	    }
223	
224	    func write(_ secret: String) throws {
225	        lock.lock()
226	        self.secret = REDACTED
227	        lock.unlock()
228	    }
229	
230	    func remove() throws {
231	        lock.lock()
232	        secret = nil
233	        lock.unlock()
234	    }
235	}

3	/// AssemblyAI's REST API, as five synchronous methods — road map 6 §5c
4	/// whole. Foundation only: no AppKit, no document, nothing about a project,
5	/// so a probe drives it against the stand-in server over a socket and, for
6	/// the retry and backoff rules, against an injected `URLProtocol` with no
7	/// socket at all.
8	///
9	/// **R6-7: no `async`.** Each method builds a task and waits on a semaphore
10	/// the delegate signals — the shape the old on-device `TaskSink` had, and
11	/// the delegate queue is one of ours for its reason: the framework's default
12	/// would make an off-main tool's wait depend on somebody else's queue staying
13	/// free.
14	///
15	/// **A redirect is never followed.** `willPerformHTTPRedirection` always
16	/// answers nil, so the 3xx is delivered as the task's own response and comes
17	/// back as `.redirected`. Following one would re-send the `authorization`
18	/// header to whatever host the `Location` named — the spike's Python client
19	/// needed a `NoRedirect` handler for exactly this.
20	///
21	/// **The credential is in one header and in no log line.** A log line carries
22	/// a method, a path and a status; the session is `.ephemeral` with its
23	/// cookie, cache and credential storage cleared, so the framework writes
24	/// nothing about a request to disk either.
25	final class AssemblyAIClient {
26	
27	    /// The numbers road map 6 §8 says a person may want to change, in one
28	    /// value a probe can replace wholesale.
29	    struct Tuning: Equatable {
30	        /// Seconds between polls — AssemblyAI's own SDKs' default.
31	        var pollInterval: TimeInterval
32	        /// The poll ceiling never falls below this, however short the audio.
33	        var pollCeilingFloor: TimeInterval
34	        /// Audio seconds per second of ceiling: floor(147 ÷ 3) from C0's q8,
35	        /// which measured an hour completing in 24.4 s — three times the
36	        /// measured rate is the margin a queue can eat.
37	        var pollCeilingDivisor: Double
38	        /// One retry: a dropped socket's worth, and two uploads of a 100 MB
39	        /// file are the cost of a third.
40	        var uploadRetries: Int
41	        var retryBackoff: TimeInterval
42	        /// Consecutive 5xx or transport errors a poll loop tolerates.
43	        var pollFailuresTolerated: Int
44	        /// The janitor's budget per item; the slowest DELETE C0 timed was
45	        /// 1.70 s.
46	        var deleteTimeout: TimeInterval
47	        /// Every other request's ceiling.
48	        var requestTimeout: TimeInterval
49	        /// Looks at the newest transcript page after an ambiguous submit.
50	        var submitRecoveryAttempts: Int = 3
51	        var submitRecoveryDelay: TimeInterval = 2.5
52	        var submitRecoveryTimeout: TimeInterval = 5
53	        /// How long a DELETE runs on after a Stop, in wall clock from the
54	        /// later of the Stop and its own start (R6-19): above C0's slowest
55	        /// DELETE, so a Stop during a submit or a wait still deletes.
56	        var deleteAfterStop: TimeInterval = 2
57	
58	        static let shipped = Tuning(
59	            pollInterval: 3, pollCeilingFloor: 300, pollCeilingDivisor: 49, uploadRetries: 1,
60	            retryBackoff: 1, pollFailuresTolerated: 3, deleteTimeout: 5, requestTimeout: 60)
61	
62	        /// `max(300 s, audio seconds / 49)` — §8's row.
63	        func pollCeiling(audioSeconds: Double) -> TimeInterval {
64	            guard pollCeilingDivisor > 0 else { return pollCeilingFloor }
65	            return max(pollCeilingFloor, audioSeconds / pollCeilingDivisor)
66	        }
67	    }

70	    /// minutes of processing at q8's rate, and 550 MB of FLAC.
71	    static let maxMediaSeconds = 36_000
72	    /// `keyterms_prompt`'s documented ceiling on Universal-3.5 Pro.

172	    /// `POST /v2/upload` — the body streams from the file and is never in
173	    /// memory. One retry on a transport error or a 5xx, none on a 4xx.
174	    func upload(
175	        file: URL, cancel: Transcriber.CancelToken? = nil,
176	        progress: ((Int64, Int64) -> Void)? = nil
177	    ) throws -> URL {
178	        var request = self.request("POST", path: "/v2/upload")
179	        request.setValue("application/octet-stream", forHTTPHeaderField: "content-type")
180	        var attempt = 0
181	        while true {
182	            if cancel?.isCancelled == true { throw ClientError.cancelled }
183	            let reply = send(request, file: file, cancel: cancel, progress: progress)
184	            if let failure = classify(reply) {
185	                guard failure.isRetriable, attempt < tuning.uploadRetries,
186	                    cancel?.isCancelled != true
187	                else { throw failure }
188	                attempt += 1
189	                note("retry \(attempt) of upload after \(failure.shortName)")
190	                sleep(tuning.retryBackoff, cancel: cancel)
191	                continue
192	            }
193	            guard
194	                let object = try? JSONSerialization.jsonObject(with: reply.data)
195	                    as? [String: Any], let text = object["upload_url"] as? String,
196	                let url = URL(string: text)
197	            else { throw ClientError.malformed("the upload answered no `upload_url`") }
198	            return url
199	        }
200	    }

202	    /// `GET /v2/transcript/{id}` every `pollInterval` until it is
203	    /// `completed`, it is `error`, the ceiling passes or the token is
204	    /// cancelled.
205	    ///
206	    /// **Every throwing exit deletes the transcript first** (R6-4): one
207	    /// `delete(id:cancel:)`, best effort, before the throw. A transcript AssemblyAI
208	    /// is still making, or has made and nobody read, is one it keeps
209	    /// indefinitely, and this is the one place that knows its id.
210	    ///
211	    /// **A `completed` body with no words array is `.malformed`, never an
212	    /// empty transcript.** `[]` is an array and means zero words, a real
213	    /// answer about audio nobody spoke in; an absent `words`, a `null` one
214	    /// and an object are bodies this client cannot read, and turning one into
215	    /// "nothing was said" would cache a broken response as a fact.
216	    func poll(
217	        id: String, audioSeconds: Double, cancel: Transcriber.CancelToken? = nil,
218	        waited: ((TimeInterval) -> Void)? = nil
219	    ) throws -> Fetched {
220	        guard isSendableIdentifier(id) else {
221	            throw ClientError.malformed("AssemblyAI answered an id that is not one")
222	        }
223	        let ceiling = tuning.pollCeiling(audioSeconds: audioSeconds)
224	        let started = Date()
225	        var failures = 0
226	        while true {
227	            if cancel?.isCancelled == true { throw refusing(.cancelled, id: id, cancel: cancel) }
228	            if Date().timeIntervalSince(started) > ceiling {
229	                throw refusing(.timedOut, id: id, cancel: cancel)
230	            }
231	            let reply = send(request("GET", path: "/v2/transcript/\(id)"), cancel: cancel)
232	            if let failure = classify(reply) {
233	                guard failure.isRetriable else { throw refusing(failure, id: id, cancel: cancel) }
234	                failures += 1
235	                note("poll \(id) failed (\(failure.shortName)), \(failures) in a row")
236	                if failures > tuning.pollFailuresTolerated {
237	                    throw refusing(failure, id: id, cancel: cancel)
238	                }
239	            } else {
240	                failures = 0
241	                guard
242	                    let response = try? JSONDecoder().decode(
243	                        TranscriptResponse.self, from: reply.data)
244	                else {
245	                    throw refusing(
246	                        .malformed("the transcript did not decode"), id: id, cancel: cancel)
247	                }
248	                if response.status == "error" {
249	                    throw refusing(
250	                        .transcript(
251	                            relayed(
252	                                response.error ?? "AssemblyAI could not transcribe it")),
253	                        id: id, cancel: cancel)
254	                }
255	                if response.status == "completed" {
256	                    try requireEchoedID(response, polled: id, cancel: cancel)
257	                    guard let words = wordsBytes(in: reply.data) else {
258	                        throw refusing(
259	                            .malformed("the transcript came back completed with no words array"),
260	                            id: id, cancel: cancel)
261	                    }
262	                    return Fetched(response: response, wordsJSON: words)
263	                }
264	            }
265	            waited?(Date().timeIntervalSince(started))
266	            sleep(tuning.pollInterval, cancel: cancel)
267	        }
268	    }

271	    /// that interpolate one into a path go through.
272	    ///
273	    /// An id reaches this client from two places that are not this app: the
274	    /// `transcript_id` of a cache file, which rides inside a `.framejob`
275	    /// package and can be hand-edited or authored by somebody else, and a
276	    /// submission's own reply. `URL.appendingPathComponent` does not resolve
277	    /// `..` and `URLSession` sends the path as written, so
278	    /// `"transcript_id": "../../v1/anything"` in a package made a DELETE go
279	    /// to a path of its author's choosing on the API host, carrying the
280	    /// person's key (the reader review, road map 6 §10.13, R3·1). Letters,
281	    /// digits, `-` and `_` are what the service's own ids are made of, and a
282	    /// bounded length is what keeps a megabyte of them off the wire.
283	    static func isPlainIdentifier(_ id: String) -> Bool {
284	        guard !id.isEmpty, id.count <= 128 else { return false }
285	        return id.allSatisfy { $0.isASCII && ($0.isLetter || $0.isNumber || $0 == "-" || $0 == "_") }
286	    }
287	
288	    /// What one DELETE answered. THREE states, because "never sent" is
289	    /// neither "gone" nor "owed" (the reader review's fix pass, §10.13).
290	    enum DeleteAnswer { case deleted, failed, notSent }
291	
292	    /// `DELETE /v2/transcript/{id}` on `deleteTimeout`. Best effort by
293	    /// design: a `failed` delete is RECORDED in the cache file and retried by
294	    /// the next run's janitor, and a repeat answers 200 (q6), so a retry
295	    /// cannot make things worse.
296	    ///
297	    /// **An id that is not one is `notSent`, with no request at all.**
298	    /// AssemblyAI cannot have minted it, so there is nothing to delete;
299	    /// `failed` would put the media in `janitorFailed` and R6-11 would HOLD
300	    /// it for ever over a string, and `deleted` would report — and write into
301	    /// the cache file — a delete this app never asked for.
302	    ///
303	    /// **`cancel` is read as a STOP and never attached** (R6-19). Attaching
304	    /// would cancel the DELETE at the press, orphaning the transcript of
305	    /// every Stop during a submit or a wait; instead the DELETE is cut
306	    /// `deleteAfterStop` of wall clock after the later of the Stop and its
307	    /// own start, and a cut one is `failed` — owed, as any failed one is. No
308	    /// default: every caller names the token it has, or nil.
309	    @discardableResult
310	    func delete(id: String, cancel: Transcriber.CancelToken?) -> DeleteAnswer {
311	        guard isSendableIdentifier(id) else {
312	            note("refusing to DELETE an id that is not one")
313	            return .notSent
314	        }
315	        var request = self.request("DELETE", path: "/v2/transcript/\(id)")
316	        request.timeoutInterval = tuning.deleteTimeout
317	        let reply = send(request, stop: cancel, grace: tuning.deleteAfterStop)
318	        return classify(reply) == nil ? .deleted : .failed
319	    }
320	
321	    // MARK: - One request
322	
323	    /// `request` and `send` stay in this file and not in `+Session.swift`
324	    /// because they are two of the THREE members that touch `credential`,
325	    /// `delegate` and `session`, which are `private` — and `private` on a
326	    /// stored property does not cross a file. Keeping them here is what lets
327	    /// the credential stay private rather than being widened for a size toll.
328	    /// The third is `withoutCredential(_:)` above, which the reader review
329	    /// added for the same reason and in the same place (§10.13, R2·1).
330	    func request(_ method: String, path: String, query: String? = nil) -> URLRequest {
331	        var components = URLComponents(
332	            url: base.appendingPathComponent(path), resolvingAgainstBaseURL: false)
333	        components?.query = query
334	        var request = URLRequest(url: components?.url ?? base.appendingPathComponent(path))
335	        request.httpMethod = method
336	        request.setValue(credential, forHTTPHeaderField: "authorization")
337	        request.timeoutInterval = tuning.requestTimeout
338	        return request
339	    }
340	
341	    /// Builds the task, hands the delegate its sink, waits. The wait has no
342	    /// deadline of its own but a Stop's: `timeoutIntervalForRequest` is the
343	    /// idle bound, and a second one here would leave a task running with
344	    /// nobody to read it. A token is read one of two ways: `cancel` is
345	    /// ATTACHED, so a Stop cancels the task at the press; `stop` never is —
346	    /// `waitForReply` cuts the task `grace` seconds after it is first seen
347	    /// set and still waits for its completion. Only `delete` passes a `stop`
348	    /// (R6-19).
349	    func send(
350	        _ request: URLRequest, file: URL? = nil, cancel: Transcriber.CancelToken? = nil,
351	        stop: Transcriber.CancelToken? = nil, grace: TimeInterval = 0,
352	        progress: ((Int64, Int64) -> Void)? = nil
353	    ) -> Reply {
354	        let task =
355	            file.map { session.uploadTask(with: request, fromFile: $0) }
356	            ?? session.dataTask(with: request)
357	        let sink = delegate.open(task.taskIdentifier, progress: progress)
358	        cancel?.attach(task)
359	        task.resume()
360	        waitForReply(sink.done, task: task, stop: stop, grace: grace)
361	        cancel?.release()
362	        let reply = delegate.close(task.taskIdentifier)
363	        note("\(request.httpMethod ?? "?") \(request.url?.path ?? "?") → "
364	            + "\(reply.response?.statusCode.description ?? reply.error.map { _ in "error" } ?? "?")")
365	        return reply
366	    }
367	
368	    /// A sentence the SERVER wrote, with this client's own credential taken
369	    /// out of it.
370	    ///
371	    /// Three sentences are relayed as the service wrote them — a 402's, a
372	    /// 4xx's and a transcript's `error` — as AssemblyAI says the useful thing
373	    /// (R6-6); `relayed` (`+Session`) filters each here, then bounds it
374	    /// (R6-23). But that text is somebody ELSE's, and a server echoing the
375	    /// `authorization` header it received puts the key in it: a stand-in
376	    /// answering `400 … for <the key>` put the credential straight into an
377	    /// MCP refusal, which `AgentServer+CloudCaptions.swift`'s header promises
378	    /// never happens (the reader review, road map 6 §10.13, R2·1). This is
379	    /// the one place that can know the string to look for, because
380	    /// `credential` is `private` and does not cross a file.
381	    func withoutCredential(_ text: String) -> String {
382	        guard !credential.isEmpty, text.contains(credential) else { return text }
383	        return text.replacingOccurrences(of: credential, with: "<redacted>")
384	    }
385	
386	    /// `GET /v2/transcript?limit=1` — the cheapest authenticated call, for
387	    /// the Settings window's Verify button.
388	    func verify() -> Result<Void, ClientError> {
389	        let reply = send(request("GET", path: "/v2/transcript", query: "limit=1"))
390	        if let failure = classify(reply) { return .failure(failure) }
391	        return .success(())
392	    }
393	}

5	/// What a reply MEANS and who delivers it: `Reply`, the status classifier,
6	/// the two readers that cut a served body apart, the one-delete-then-throw
7	/// helper and the `Refusal` it answers (R6-20), the cancellable wait, the
8	/// wait for a reply that a Stop bounds (`waitForReply`, R6-19), the log
9	/// line — and `SessionDelegate`, the object `URLSession` calls back on its
10	/// own one-wide queue. At the foot,
11	/// `ClientError`'s two readings, `isRetriable` and `shortName`: a pure move
12	/// out of `AssemblyAIClient.swift`, which stood at 399 lines against the
13	/// cap when a DELETE learned to read a Stop (issue batch B35).
14	///
15	/// It is beside `AssemblyAIClient.swift` rather than in it because that file
16	/// holds road map 6 §5c's five calls and §8's numbers and stood at 487 lines
17	/// with this in it, against the 400-line cap on a new file (app/CLAUDE.md,
18	/// road map 6 §5h). The split is the one the spec already made for
19	/// `AssemblyAITranscript.swift`, one seam further along: the wire VALUES
20	/// left first, then the wire MACHINERY, so what is left in the client file
21	/// is the five calls a reader came for.
22	///
23	/// `request` and `send` did NOT come here, and neither did
24	/// `withoutCredential(_:)`. Those three are the members that touch
25	/// `credential`, `delegate` and `session`, and `private` on a stored property
26	/// does not cross a file: moving them would have widened the credential to
27	/// pay a size toll, which is the wrong direction. `classify` below CALLS
28	/// `withoutCredential` and does not name the credential itself.
29	extension AssemblyAIClient {
30	
31	    struct Reply {
32	        var data = Data()
33	        var response: HTTPURLResponse?
34	        var error: (any Error)?
35	    }
36	
37	    /// The status a reply carries, as an error or nil. A redirect arrives
38	    /// as a 3xx because the delegate refused to follow it.
39	    func classify(_ reply: Reply) -> ClientError? {
40	        if let error = reply.error as? URLError {
41	            switch error.code {
42	            case .cancelled: return .cancelled
43	            case .timedOut: return .timedOut
44	            default: return .noNetwork
45	            }
46	        }
47	        if reply.error != nil { return .noNetwork }
48	        guard let response = reply.response else {
49	            return .malformed("the request answered nothing at all")
50	        }
51	        let code = response.statusCode
52	        switch code {
53	        case 200..<300: return nil
54	        case 300..<400: return .redirected(code)
55	        case 401, 403: return .keyRefused(code)
56	        case 402:
57	            return .account(
58	                relayed(sentence(in: reply.data) ?? "AssemblyAI answered \(code)"))
59	        case 400..<500:
60	            return .request(
61	                relayed(sentence(in: reply.data) ?? "AssemblyAI answered \(code)"))
62	        default: return .server(code)
63	        }
64	    }
65	
66	    /// AssemblyAI's own `error` sentence out of a body, relayed as the
67	    /// service wrote it — through `relayed`, which takes this client's key
68	    /// out and then bounds it (R6-23), so the promise is about the SERVER's
69	    /// words and not about this client's key or an endless body.
70	    private func sentence(in data: Data) -> String? {
71	        guard let object = try? JSONSerialization.jsonObject(with: data) as? [String: Any],
72	            let text = object["error"] as? String, !text.isEmpty
73	        else { return nil }
74	        return text
75	    }
76	
77	    /// The most Unicode scalars a sentence the SERVER wrote — a 402's, a
78	    /// 4xx's, a transcript's `error` — keeps where the app relays it
79	    /// (R6-23). A ceiling against a broken or hostile server, not a measured
80	    /// length.
81	    static let relayedSentenceLimit = 300
82	
83	    /// At most `limit` Unicode scalars: a longer string is its first
84	    /// `limit - 1` scalars + "…" (U+2026). The one scalar cutter — the
85	    /// relayed sentences here, and `CloudTranscriber.bounded`'s model and
86	    /// language (R6-23).
87	    static func bounded(_ text: String, limit: Int) -> String {
88	        let scalars = text.unicodeScalars
89	        guard scalars.count > limit else { return text }
90	        var kept = String.UnicodeScalarView(scalars.prefix(limit - 1))
91	        kept.append("\u{2026}")
92	        return String(kept)
93	    }
94	
95	    /// A sentence the server wrote, as the app relays it: the key filtered
96	    /// out FIRST, then cut, so a cut never splits the key into a piece the
97	    /// filter cannot see (R6-23).
98	    func relayed(_ text: String) -> String {
99	        Self.bounded(withoutCredential(text), limit: Self.relayedSentenceLimit)
100	    }
101	
102	    /// The served bytes of a top-level `words` ARRAY, or nil when the key is
103	    /// absent, does not begin `[`, or will not decode as words.
104	    func wordsBytes(in body: Data) -> Data? {
105	        guard let range = JSONValueRange.topLevel(key: "words", in: body) else { return nil }
106	        let bytes = body.subdata(in: range)
107	        guard bytes.first == UInt8(ascii: "[") else { return nil }
108	        guard (try? JSONDecoder().decode([TranscriptWord].self, from: bytes)) != nil else {
109	            return nil
110	        }
111	        return bytes
112	    }
113	
114	    /// Whether `text` repeats this client's own credential — the question
115	    /// `withoutCredential` answers by changing the text, asked without it.
116	    func carriesCredential(_ text: String) -> Bool {
117	        withoutCredential(text) != text
118	    }
119	
120	    /// The ONE gate for a transcript id this client puts in a path (`poll`,
121	    /// `delete`) or accepts from a submit reply or a recovery-list row: plain
122	    /// (`isPlainIdentifier`) AND not the credential. An id that repeats the
123	    /// key would put it in a request path and a log line, so it is never
124	    /// sent and never accepted (#187, R2·1).
125	    func isSendableIdentifier(_ id: String) -> Bool {
126	        Self.isPlainIdentifier(id) && !carriesCredential(id)
127	    }
128	
129	    /// A transcript refused after AssemblyAI made it, and what refusing's
130	    /// DELETE of it answered (#201, R6-20). It reads as `failure`'s own
131	    /// sentence; `CloudTranscriber.transcribe` records a `failed` deletion
132	    /// in `Report.refusedUndeleted` and then reads `failure` alone.
133	    struct Refusal: LocalizedError, Equatable {
134	        let failure: ClientError
135	        let deletion: DeleteAnswer
136	
137	        var errorDescription: String? { failure.errorDescription }
138	    }
139	
140	    /// One `delete` before a throw, and the error to throw, carrying that
141	    /// delete's answer.
142	    func refusing(
143	        _ failure: ClientError, id: String, cancel: Transcriber.CancelToken?
144	    ) -> Refusal {
145	        Refusal(failure: failure, deletion: delete(id: id, cancel: cancel))
146	    }
147	
148	    /// A `completed` body must name the id that was polled, or it is
149	    /// `.malformed` (#71).
150	    ///
151	    /// `fetch` stores `response.id` in the cache file and later deletes it,
152	    /// so a body served under another id — `../upload`, or a plain id that
153	    /// is somebody else's — would be cached and promised a retry that can
154	    /// never be sent, or would move the DELETE to a transcript this run
155	    /// never made. Refusing here keeps the id `fetch` stores and deletes the
156	    /// submitted one, and `refusing` deletes the POLLED id, which is plain.
157	    func requireEchoedID(
158	        _ response: TranscriptResponse, polled id: String, cancel: Transcriber.CancelToken?
159	    ) throws {
160	        guard response.id != id else { return }
161	        throw refusing(
162	            .malformed(
163	                "the transcript came back completed under an id other than the one polled"),
164	            id: id, cancel: cancel)
165	    }
166	
167	    /// Waits in slices of at most a tenth of a second, reading the token
168	    /// between them, so a cancel during a three-second gap is acted on in a
169	    /// tenth rather than at the next poll.
170	    func sleep(_ seconds: TimeInterval, cancel: Transcriber.CancelToken?) {
171	        var left = seconds
172	        while left > 0 {
173	            if cancel?.isCancelled == true { return }
174	            let slice = min(0.1, left)
175	            Thread.sleep(forTimeInterval: slice)
176	            left -= slice
177	        }
178	    }
179	
180	    /// Waits for `done`, and with a `stop` token bounds the wait (R6-19).
181	    /// The token is read at the start and after every slice of at most a
182	    /// tenth of a second; once `grace` seconds of wall clock have passed
183	    /// since the first reading that saw it set, the task is cancelled and
184	    /// its completion — which a cancel always delivers — is waited for, so
185	    /// no task is left running with nobody to read it. Wall clock, because a
186	    /// server that drips resets the idle timeout on every byte (R6-18). No
187	    /// `stop` is `done.wait()`, exactly as before. No queue, timer or
188	    /// thread: `sleep(_:cancel:)`'s slices, on the calling thread.
189	    func waitForReply(
190	        _ done: DispatchSemaphore, task: URLSessionTask, stop: Transcriber.CancelToken?,
191	        grace: TimeInterval
192	    ) {
193	        guard let stop else {
194	            done.wait()
195	            return
196	        }
197	        var stoppedAt: Date? = stop.isCancelled ? Date() : nil
198	        while true {
199	            if let stoppedAt, Date().timeIntervalSince(stoppedAt) >= grace {
200	                task.cancel()
201	                done.wait()
202	                return
203	            }
204	            if done.wait(timeout: .now() + 0.1) == .success { return }
205	            if stoppedAt == nil, stop.isCancelled { stoppedAt = Date() }
206	        }
207	    }
208	
209	    /// A method, a path and a status. Never a header and never a body:
210	    /// `authorization` is in one, a signed URL may be in the other. Named
211	    /// `note` rather than `log` because Darwin's `log(_:)` is a global
212	    /// function on `Double` and an unqualified `log("…")` resolves to it.
213	    ///
214	    /// Written straight to fd 1 through `FileHandle.standardOutput`, never
215	    /// `print` (#116): `print` is block-buffered (4096 B) under a file
216	    /// redirect, so an instance log held only the lines before the last full
217	    /// block. The throwing `write(contentsOf:)` because the legacy
218	    /// `write(_:)` raises an Objective-C exception on a bad descriptor.
219	    func note(_ line: String) {
220	        try? FileHandle.standardOutput.write(contentsOf: Data("AssemblyAI: \(line)\n".utf8))
221	    }
