1	import AppKit
2	
3	/// `transcribe`'s CLOUD arm — road map 6 §5g. The engine argument, the three
4	/// arguments that only mean something with it, and the run itself.
5	///
6	/// It is a file of its own, and `AgentServer+Captions.swift` is otherwise the
7	/// code it was, for the reason §5g gives: the on-device path's refusals are a
8	/// story about an installed MODEL, the cloud path's are a story
9	/// about a CREDENTIAL and somebody else's service, and the two read as one
10	/// tangle when they are interleaved. What the two share — the scope, the
11	/// jobs, the frame, the cues, `CaptionLayout.place` and the result's shape —
12	/// stays over there and is reached exactly once from here, through this
13	/// method's two arguments and its answer.
14	///
15	/// **R6-2: `engine` is never remembered.** `TranscriptionEngine.defaultsKey`
16	/// is the SHEET's memory of what a person last chose, and this file does not
17	/// read it. An agent that wants its audio uploaded says so every time, which
18	/// is the only shape in which a call's meaning does not depend on what
19	/// somebody did in the UI an hour ago.
20	///
21	/// **R6-7: no `async`, and no queue of its own.** `CloudTranscriber.transcribe`
22	/// is the SYNCHRONOUS body, and this handler is already off main
23	/// (`AgentServer.offMainTools`), so the run happens on the server thread and
24	/// the wait IS the call — `transcribe`'s own argument for why it is in that
25	/// set, read across to an engine that waits on a socket instead of on a
26	/// recogniser.
27	///
28	/// **No credential is ever in an answer.** Not in a `ToolError`, not in a
29	/// `Problem`, not in the `note`: the only thing this file does with the
30	/// credential is hand it to `AssemblyAIClient.init`, which puts it in one
31	/// header and in no log line.
32	///
33	/// **R6-12, stated here because this is where it would be broken.** The KEY
34	/// and the REGION are a person's settings and no tool reads or writes
35	/// either: the key is R6-5's rule, and the region is a default a person sets
36	/// in the Settings window's Transcription pane, and it decides only WHERE a
37	/// transcript is made. So this file resolves both through
38	/// `AssemblyAIConfiguration` and offers neither as an argument, and
39	/// `cloudFields` names no region — every proof instance runs under
40	/// `-RCAssemblyAIEndpoint`, where the region is not where the run spoke, so
41	/// the key could be proved only where it is false. The honest shape is the
42	/// one that has landed (#94): the run's client's HOST alone, under a key
43	/// named `endpoint` — a fact about where the requests went, never an
44	/// argument.
45	/// The vocabulary's rules are `TranscriptOptions.keyterms`, the one spelling
46	/// the sheet shares (c1-chrome moved them there verbatim).
47	extension AgentServer {
48	
49	    // MARK: - The engine argument
50	
51	    /// `engine`, refused BY NAME with both spellings when it is neither.
52	    ///
53	    /// Absent is `.apple`, and absent is the ONLY thing that makes it
54	    /// `.apple`: `UserDefaults` is not consulted here (R6-2). It is read
55	    /// through `stringArg`, so a number or an object is refused as a type
56	    /// error naming the key before the spelling is even looked at.
57	    func transcriptionEngine(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> TranscriptionEngine {
58	        guard let name = try stringArg(a, "engine") else { return .apple }
59	        guard let engine = TranscriptionEngine(rawValue: name) else {
60	            throw ToolError(
61	                message: "engine must be \"apple\" or \"assemblyai\" (got \"\(name)\").")
62	        }
63	        return engine
64	    }
65	
66	    /// The three arguments that only mean something to AssemblyAI, refused
67	    /// by name under `engine: "apple"`.
68	    ///
69	    /// `voice_confidence`-with-`mode: "level"`'s precedent (road map 4):
70	    /// an argument that cannot do anything is a MISTAKE, not a no-op, and
71	    /// dropping it quietly would let a caller believe a speaker-labelled
72	    /// transcript had been asked for and read the cues as if it had. The
73	    /// FIRST one present is the one named, in a fixed order, so the refusal
74	    /// is the same sentence for the same call every time.
75	    func refuseCloudOnlyArguments(_ a: [String: Any]) throws {
76	        for key in ["speakers", "vocabulary", "refresh"] {
77	            guard let value = a[key], !(value is NSNull) else { continue }
78	            throw ToolError(
79	                message: "\(key) only applies with engine \"assemblyai\". Pass engine: "
80	                    + "\"assemblyai\", or leave it out.")
81	        }
82	    }
83	
84	    // MARK: - The cloud run
85	
86	    /// The whole of the cloud arm: the three arguments, the vocabulary's
87	    /// rules, the credential, the endpoint, the run, and the result keys
88	    /// `Outcome` has no room for.
89	    ///
90	    /// **The refusal order is §5g's**, and every step of it is above the
91	    /// network on purpose. The caller's own mistakes are already answered by
92	    /// the time this is called (unknown clip, empty scope, misspelt engine);
93	    /// here it is the arguments' own types and values, then the CREDENTIAL,
94	    /// then the endpoint — and only then is a socket opened. A run that was
95	    /// going to be refused for a missing key must not first extract and
96	    /// upload half a gigabyte of audio to find that out.
97	    ///
98	    /// **The main thread is touched exactly once**, for the document's cache
99	    /// directory and its media records. Everything else the run needs is in
100	    /// the `Job`s by value, which is what lets the whole round trip happen
101	    /// off main with no document held.
102	    func cloudTranscription(
103	        _ a: [String: Any], document: ProjectDocument, jobs: [Transcriber.Job], frame: Ticks,
104	        pages: CaptionPages.Request, language: String?
105	    ) throws -> (outcome: Transcriber.Outcome, fields: [String: Any]) {
106	        let speakers = try boolArg(a, "speakers") ?? false
107	        let asked = try stringsArg(a, "vocabulary") ?? []
108	        let refresh = try boolArg(a, "refresh") ?? false
109	        let code = try Self.cloudLanguage(language)
110	        let vocabulary = TranscriptOptions.keyterms(asked)
111	
112	        var notes: [String] = []
113	        if asked.count > vocabulary.count, vocabulary.count == AssemblyAIClient.maxKeyterms {
114	            notes.append(
115	                "vocabulary was capped at \(AssemblyAIClient.maxKeyterms) terms (AssemblyAI's "
116	                    + "limit); \(asked.count) were given.")
117	        }
118	
119	        let credential = AssemblyAIConfiguration.credential(
120	            store: AssemblyAIConfiguration.store())
121	        var client: AssemblyAIClient?
122	        if let credential {
123	            do {
124	                let base = try AssemblyAIConfiguration.baseURL()
125	                client = AssemblyAIClient(base: base, credential: credential)
126	            } catch {
127	                throw ToolError(message: error.localizedDescription)
128	            }
129	        }
130	
131	        let context = try onMain { () -> (cache: URL, media: [UInt32: MediaSnapshot]) in
132	            guard let cache = document.cacheDirectory else {
133	                throw ToolError(
134	                    message: "This document has nowhere to keep its transcript cache, so it "
135	                        + "cannot be transcribed with AssemblyAI. Save it first.")
136	            }
137	            var records: [UInt32: MediaSnapshot] = [:]
138	            for entry in document.editedProject.snapshot.media { records[entry.id] = entry }
139	            return (cache, records)
140	        }
141	
142	        let options = TranscriptOptions(
143	            speechModels: TranscriptOptions.shippedModels, languageCode: code,
144	            speakerLabels: speakers, keytermsPrompt: vocabulary)
145	        let transcriber = CloudTranscriber(
146	            client: client,
147	            cacheDirectory: context.cache, media: context.media)
148	        let outcome: Transcriber.Outcome
149	        do {
150	            outcome = try transcriber.transcribe(
151	                jobs, options: options, refresh: refresh, frame: frame, pages: pages,
152	                cancel: Transcriber.CancelToken())
153	        } catch {
154	            // In band, message and all, exactly as the on-device arm does —
155	            // including "no speech was recognised", which is a true answer
156	            // about the audio rather than a transport problem.
157	            //
158	            // **A throw that came AFTER a bill says so.** `cloudFields` is
159	            // never reached on this path, so `uploaded` and `audio_seconds`
160	            // are not in the answer at all: a run whose only media held no
161	            // speech, or whose second media answered 401, told the caller
162	            // nothing about the money already spent (the reader review,
163	            // §10.13, R5·2). The facts go in the SENTENCE, which is the one
164	            // channel a throw has; the result KEYS are unchanged.
165	            throw ToolError(message: Self.cloudFailure(error, report: transcriber.report))
166	        }
167	        return (
168	            outcome,
169	            Self.cloudFields(transcriber.report, code: code, endpoint: client?.base.host, notes: notes)
170	        )
171	    }
172	
173	    /// What a FAILED run already cost, as a sentence to put after the
174	    /// failure's own — or nothing at all when it cost nothing.
175	    ///
176	    /// Only the media AssemblyAI actually answered for are counted:
177	    /// `report.uploaded` is written once per media that came back, so a media
178	    /// the run refused or could not reach is not in it.
179	    ///
180	    /// **It promises nothing about the cache.** It used to close with "their
181	    /// transcripts are cached in the project, so another run makes no request
182	    /// for them", which is false on the branch R1·3's fix created and issue
183	    /// #29 records: when `MediaTranscript.write` answers `false` the marker is
184	    /// (correctly) not written and NOTHING is cached, while the media is in
185	    /// `report.uploaded` all the same — so a caller who believed the sentence
186	    /// paid for the same media twice. The bill is what this method knows;
187	    /// what landed in the cache is not (the reader review's fix pass,
188	    /// §10.13).
189	    static func billed(_ report: CloudTranscriber.Report) -> String {
190	        guard !report.uploaded.isEmpty else { return "" }
191	        let seconds = report.billedSeconds
192	        let files = report.uploaded.count == 1 ? "1 media file" : "\(report.uploaded.count) media files"
193	        return " AssemblyAI had already been billed for \(files) (\(seconds) audio seconds) "
194	            + "before this failed."
195	    }
196	
197	    static func cloudFailure(_ error: any Error, report: CloudTranscriber.Report) -> String {
198	        let warnings = report.deletionWarnings { "media \($0)" }
199	            + report.cacheWarnings { "media \($0)" }
200	        return ([error.localizedDescription + billed(report)] + warnings)
201	            .joined(separator: "\n")
202	    }
203	
204	    /// `language` for the cloud engine: absent or `"auto"` is DETECTION,
205	    /// which is the wire's absent `language_code`; anything else is passed
206	    /// through trimmed.
207	    ///
208	    /// Nothing here checks the code against a table. C0's q5 measured that a
209	    /// code AssemblyAI does not support is a 400 at SUBMISSION in 0.24 s with
210	    /// its own sentence — so the cost of a wrong code is one wasted upload,
211	    /// and relaying the service's answer is better than carrying a second
212	    /// dated list of codes that can be wrong in the other direction. An
213	    /// EMPTY string is refused here, though: it is not a code and it is not
214	    /// "auto", and sending it would be asking for a language called "".
215	    private static func cloudLanguage(_ wanted: String?) throws -> String? {
216	        guard let wanted = wanted else { return nil }
217	        let trimmed = wanted.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
218	        guard !trimmed.isEmpty else {
219	            throw ToolError(
220	                message: "language cannot be empty. Pass a code like en, or \"auto\" to let "
221	                    + "AssemblyAI detect it, or leave it out.")
222	        }
223	        return trimmed.lowercased() == "auto" ? nil : trimmed
224	    }
225	
226	    /// The result keys the cloud engine adds — §5g's list, built from the
227	    /// run's own `Report` and from nothing else.
228	    ///
229	    /// `note` exists only when there is a part to put in it: R6-8's fallback
230	    /// ran, a vocabulary was cut, a remote delete is still owed, or a
231	    /// fetched transcript could not be kept for reuse. An empty
232	    /// note would be a key a caller has to read to learn nothing.
233	    ///
234	    /// `endpoint` is the HOST alone of the base URL the run's client spoke
235	    /// to (#94) — no scheme, port, path or userinfo, so no credential can
236	    /// ride in it (R6-5) — and it is absent when there was no client: a
237	    /// keyless run found no credential, built none, and sent nothing.
238	    static func cloudFields(
239	        _ report: CloudTranscriber.Report, code: String?, endpoint: String?, notes: [String]
240	    ) -> [String: Any] {
241	        var parts = notes
242	        let preferred = TranscriptOptions.shippedModels.first ?? "universal-3-5-pro"
243	        for row in report.uploaded {
244	            guard let model = row.speechModelUsed, model != preferred else { continue }
245	            parts.append(
246	                "AssemblyAI transcribed media \(row.media) with \(model), not \(preferred).")
247	        }
248	        parts.append(contentsOf: report.deletionWarnings { "media \($0)" })
249	        parts.append(contentsOf: report.cacheWarnings { "media \($0)" })
250	
251	        var fields: [String: Any] = [
252	            "engine": TranscriptionEngine.assemblyai.rawValue,
253	            "language": code ?? "auto",
254	            "uploaded": report.uploaded.map { Int($0.media) },
255	            "cached": report.cached.map { Int($0) },
256	            "audio_seconds": report.billedSeconds,
257	        ]
258	        let models: [[String: Any]] = report.uploaded.compactMap { row in
259	            guard let model = row.speechModelUsed else { return nil }
260	            return ["media": Int(row.media), "model": model]
261	        }
262	        if !models.isEmpty { fields["speech_model_used"] = models }
263	        // Only under detection: a code the caller NAMED comes back as itself
264	        // and reporting it as "detected" would be a false claim about how it
265	        // was arrived at (C0's q1 measured that `language_confidence` is
266	        // present only when the language was detected).
267	        if code == nil {
268	            let detected: [[String: Any]] = report.uploaded.compactMap { row in
269	                guard let answer = row.languageCode else { return nil }
270	                var out: [String: Any] = ["media": Int(row.media), "code": answer]
271	                if let confidence = row.languageConfidence { out["confidence"] = confidence }
272	                return out
273	            }
274	            if !detected.isEmpty { fields["language_detected"] = detected }
275	        }
276	        if let endpoint { fields["endpoint"] = endpoint }
277	        if !parts.isEmpty { fields["note"] = parts.joined(separator: " ") }
278	        return fields
279	    }
280	}

1	import Foundation
2	
3	// MARK: - The marker
4	
5	/// The four source facts that identify audio for transcription (R6-15).
6	/// `CacheStamp` also contains display and generator fields, which remain
7	/// relevant to their own caches but cannot invalidate a transcript.
8	struct TranscriptSourceStamp: Codable, Equatable {
9	    let size: Int64
10	    let modified: Int64
11	    let duration: Ticks
12	    let hasAudio: Bool
13	
14	    init(_ source: MediaImporter.CacheStamp) {
15	        size = source.size
16	        modified = source.modified
17	        duration = source.duration
18	        hasAudio = source.hasAudio
19	    }
20	}
21	
22	/// What `cache/transcripts/<id>.complete.json` holds: the four-field source
23	/// identity plus the REQUEST. Keyed decoding projects old wide markers onto
24	/// this value, so their display-cache fields cannot cause a new upload.
25	///
26	/// The region is deliberately NOT in it. A transcript of a file is the same
27	/// whichever of AssemblyAI's two regions made it, and putting the region here
28	/// would re-upload every media of every project the first time somebody
29	/// looked at the popup.
30	struct TranscriptStamp: Codable, Equatable {
31	    let source: TranscriptSourceStamp
32	    let provider: String
33	    let speechModels: [String]
34	    let languageCode: String?
35	    let speakerLabels: Bool
36	    let keytermsPrompt: [String]
37	    /// Whether the request asked for fillers (TR-1). A marker written
38	    /// before CT-1 has no key and reads as false (TR-2).
39	    let disfluencies: Bool
40	
41	    init(source: MediaImporter.CacheStamp, options: TranscriptOptions) {
42	        self.source = TranscriptSourceStamp(source)
43	        self.provider = MediaTranscript.provider
44	        self.speechModels = options.speechModels
45	        self.languageCode = options.languageCode
46	        self.speakerLabels = options.speakerLabels
47	        self.keytermsPrompt = options.keytermsPrompt
48	        self.disfluencies = options.disfluencies
49	    }
50	
51	    enum CodingKeys: String, CodingKey {
52	        case source
53	        case provider
54	        case speechModels = "speech_models"
55	        case languageCode = "language_code"
56	        case speakerLabels = "speaker_labels"
57	        case keytermsPrompt = "keyterms_prompt"
58	        case disfluencies
59	    }
60	
61	    /// The synthesized reading for every key a marker had before CT-1, and
62	    /// `disfluencies` absent as false, so an old marker still decodes (TR-2).
63	    init(from decoder: any Decoder) throws {
64	        let container = try decoder.container(keyedBy: CodingKeys.self)
65	        source = try container.decode(TranscriptSourceStamp.self, forKey: .source)
66	        provider = try container.decode(String.self, forKey: .provider)
67	        speechModels = try container.decode([String].self, forKey: .speechModels)
68	        languageCode = try container.decodeIfPresent(String.self, forKey: .languageCode)
69	        speakerLabels = try container.decode(Bool.self, forKey: .speakerLabels)
70	        keytermsPrompt = try container.decode([String].self, forKey: .keytermsPrompt)
71	        disfluencies = try container.decodeIfPresent(Bool.self, forKey: .disfluencies) ?? false
72	    }
73	
74	    /// Every key, always, nil as `null` — `TranscriptOptions.encode`'s
75	    /// reason. A marker that dropped `language_code` when the language was
76	    /// auto would compare unequal to one written by a build that kept it.
77	    func encode(to encoder: any Encoder) throws {
78	        var container = encoder.container(keyedBy: CodingKeys.self)
79	        try container.encode(source, forKey: .source)
80	        try container.encode(provider, forKey: .provider)
81	        try container.encode(speechModels, forKey: .speechModels)
82	        try encodeOrNull(languageCode, into: &container, forKey: .languageCode)
83	        try container.encode(speakerLabels, forKey: .speakerLabels)
84	        try container.encode(keytermsPrompt, forKey: .keytermsPrompt)
85	        try container.encode(disfluencies, forKey: .disfluencies)
86	    }
87	}
88	
89	// MARK: - What a marker serves (TR-2)
90	
91	/// What a transcript is wanted for. A caption run takes a marker whatever its
92	/// `disfluencies`; a filler run (CT-2 on) needs one that asked for fillers.
93	enum TranscriptUse: Equatable { case captions, fillers }
94	
95	extension TranscriptStamp {
96	
97	    /// `self` is the marker on disk. True when every field but `disfluencies`
98	    /// equals `wanted`'s, and the use is captions or this marker asked for
99	    /// fillers — TR-2's rule, so a transcript cached before CT-1 stays
100	    /// current for captions and nothing re-transcribes on its own.
101	    func serves(_ wanted: TranscriptStamp, for use: TranscriptUse) -> Bool {
102	        guard source == wanted.source, provider == wanted.provider,
103	            speechModels == wanted.speechModels, languageCode == wanted.languageCode,
104	            speakerLabels == wanted.speakerLabels, keytermsPrompt == wanted.keytermsPrompt
105	        else { return false }
106	        return use == .captions || disfluencies
107	    }
108	}
109	
110	/// `requested`'s reading: the synthesized behaviour for the four keys a
111	/// cache file had before CT-1, and `disfluencies` absent as false (TR-2).
112	/// Here, in an extension, so `TranscriptOptions` keeps its memberwise init.
113	extension TranscriptOptions {
114	    init(from decoder: any Decoder) throws {
115	        let keys = try decoder.container(keyedBy: CodingKeys.self)
116	        let speechModels = try keys.decode([String].self, forKey: .speechModels)
117	        let languageCode = try keys.decodeIfPresent(String.self, forKey: .languageCode)
118	        let speakerLabels = try keys.decode(Bool.self, forKey: .speakerLabels)
119	        let keytermsPrompt = try keys.decode([String].self, forKey: .keytermsPrompt)
120	        let disfluencies = try keys.decodeIfPresent(Bool.self, forKey: .disfluencies) ?? false
121	        self.init(
122	            speechModels: speechModels, languageCode: languageCode,
123	            speakerLabels: speakerLabels, keytermsPrompt: keytermsPrompt,
124	            disfluencies: disfluencies)
125	    }
126	}
127

1	import Foundation
2	
3	/// The one filler vocabulary (spec §11 TR-8) and the rule that matches a word
4	/// against it. Every caption producer's input passes through
5	/// `MediaTranscript.captionWords`, so a caption made from a transcript that
6	/// asked for fillers (TR-1) is the caption the same words make without them.
7	///
8	/// The cache keeps every served word verbatim (R6-3): this filters decoded
9	/// words only, and `wordsJSON` and `File.encoded()` never see it.
10	enum FillerWords {
11	
12	    /// TR-8's list: the tokens AssemblyAI itself names as fillers for the
13	    /// models the app requests. "uh huh" is matched by its two halves, and
14	    /// `uh-huh` as one token. Another source's fillers (TR-7) are added by
15	    /// that source's own entry.
16	    static let assemblyAI: Set<String> = [
17	        "um", "uh", "hmm", "mhm", "uh-huh", "ah", "huh", "hm", "m", "er", "erm",
18	    ]
19	
20	    /// Lowercased, then leading and trailing punctuation and whitespace
21	    /// trimmed: `"Um,"` is `"um"`, and an inner hyphen stays.
22	    static func normalized(_ text: String) -> String {

3	// MARK: - Transcriber: languages
4	
5	/// The sheet's language popup and the tool's `language` argument: the
6	/// `Language` row, the two cached lists (`languages()`, the locales whose
7	/// model is INSTALLED on this Mac; `supportedLanguages()`, every locale the
8	/// engine names, each marked installed or not), the display-name builder
9	/// behind both, and the two lookups the callers use —
10	/// `defaultLanguage(in:)` for the popup's first selection and
11	/// `language(matching:in:)` for a tag a person or an agent typed.
12	///
13	/// Since W2 (spec §11 W-8) both lists are ASKED of `SpeechEngine`
14	/// (`supportedLocales()`, `installedLocales()`), never written down, and
15	/// every identifier is BCP-47 (`en-US`) — the engine answers `en_US`, and a
16	/// raw compare between the two spellings never matches. No transcriber is
17	/// constructed per locale here: constructing one reserves its locale against
18	/// a cap of 5 (W0 q3), so the installed SET comes from `installedLocales()`
19	/// and the one model question, `SpeechEngine.isInstalled`, is asked only for
20	/// the locale a run chose.
21	extension Transcriber {
22	
23	    // MARK: - Languages
24	
25	    /// One row of the sheet's language popup, and the vocabulary the tool's
26	    /// `language` argument speaks.
27	    struct Language: Equatable {
28	        /// A BCP-47 identifier, `en-US` — never `en_US`.
29	        let identifier: String
30	        let displayName: String
31	        /// Whether this Mac has the model. The sheet marks a row that has not
32	        /// and offers its Download row; a run refuses it.
33	        let installed: Bool
34	
35	        init(identifier: String, displayName: String, installed: Bool = true) {
36	            self.identifier = identifier
37	            self.displayName = displayName
38	            self.installed = installed
39	        }
40	
41	        var locale: Locale { Locale(identifier: identifier) }
42	    }
43	
44	    private static let languageLock = NSLock()
45	    private static var cachedLanguages: [Language]?
46	    private static var cachedSupported: [Language]?
47	
48	    /// Every locale whose model is INSTALLED on this Mac, sorted by display
49	    /// name — the rows a run can use without a download. All `installed`.
50	    ///
51	    /// Cached only when NON-empty: an empty answer is what `askBound`
52	    /// expiring looks like, and remembering it would make the feature refuse
53	    /// for the rest of the session on a Mac where it works.
54	    static func languages() -> [Language] {
55	        languageLock.lock()
56	        if let cached = cachedLanguages {
57	            languageLock.unlock()
58	            return cached
59	        }
60	        languageLock.unlock()
61	
62	        let found = named(SpeechEngine.installedLocales(), installed: nil)
63	        if !found.isEmpty {
64	            languageLock.lock()
65	            cachedLanguages = found
66	            languageLock.unlock()
67	        }
68	        return found
69	    }
70	
71	    /// Every locale the ENGINE names, model installed or not — the
72	    /// unfiltered twin of `languages()`, each row's `installed` read off the
73	    /// installed SET by BCP-47 tag.
74	    ///
75	    /// There are two lists because a caller who named a language this Mac
76	    /// could not use has one of TWO problems with two different fixes.
77	    /// `en-XX` is a tag the engine has never heard of, and the fix is to
78	    /// spell it right; `fr-FR` is a tag it knows that this Mac has no model
79	    /// for, and the fix is a person pressing Download in the sheet. Told only
80	    /// "this Mac cannot recognise it", somebody with the second problem
81	    /// retypes a tag that was right all along.
82	    ///
83	    /// Cached like its twin, and an empty answer is not cached — nor is a
84	    /// list read against an EMPTY installed set, which is what the installed
85	    /// ask expiring looks like: cached, every row would read "not installed"
86	    /// for the rest of the session.
87	    static func supportedLanguages() -> [Language] {
88	        languageLock.lock()
89	        if let cached = cachedSupported {
90	            languageLock.unlock()
91	            return cached
92	        }
93	        languageLock.unlock()
94	
95	        let installed = Set(SpeechEngine.installedLocales().map { $0.identifier(.bcp47) })
96	        let found = named(SpeechEngine.supportedLocales(), installed: installed)
97	        if !found.isEmpty, !installed.isEmpty {
98	            languageLock.lock()
99	            cachedSupported = found
100	            languageLock.unlock()
101	        }
102	        return found
103	    }
104	
105	    /// Drops both caches, so the next ask reads the engine again — what the
106	    /// sheet's Download row does once a model has been installed.
107	    static func forgetLanguages() {
108	        languageLock.lock()
109	        cachedLanguages = nil
110	        cachedSupported = nil
111	        languageLock.unlock()
112	    }
113	
114	    /// Locales as rows: tagged in BCP-47, named in this Mac's own language
115	    /// and sorted by that NAME rather than by tag, because a person reads the
116	    /// name — and both lists are built here so the popup and the two
117	    /// refusals cannot spell one locale two ways. `installed` nil means every
118	    /// row is installed; otherwise a row is installed when its tag is in it.
119	    /// A locale listed twice under one tag is one row.
120	    private static func named(_ locales: [Locale], installed: Set<String>?) -> [Language] {
121	        let names = Locale.current
122	        var seen = Set<String>()
123	        return locales.compactMap { locale -> Language? in
124	            let identifier = locale.identifier(.bcp47)
125	            guard seen.insert(identifier).inserted else { return nil }
126	            return Language(
127	                identifier: identifier,
128	                displayName: names.localizedString(forIdentifier: identifier) ?? identifier,
129	                installed: installed.map { $0.contains(identifier) } ?? true)
130	        }.sorted {
131	            $0.displayName.localizedStandardCompare($1.displayName) == .orderedAscending
132	        }
133	    }
134	
135	    /// The language a run defaults to: this Mac's own, then anything sharing
136	    /// its language code, then the first row — an INSTALLED row preferred at
137	    /// each step. Compared in BCP-47 (`Locale.current.identifier` is `en_US`
138	    /// and the rows are `en-US`). Over `languages()`, where every row is
139	    /// installed, this is exact → prefix → first.
140	    static func defaultLanguage(in list: [Language]) -> Language? {
141	        let current = Locale.current.identifier(.bcp47)
142	        func exact(_ row: Language) -> Bool {
143	            row.identifier.caseInsensitiveCompare(current) == .orderedSame
144	        }
145	        if let hit = list.first(where: { exact($0) && $0.installed }) { return hit }
146	        if let hit = list.first(where: exact) { return hit }
147	        let code = Locale.current.language.languageCode?.identifier ?? ""
148	        if !code.isEmpty {
149	            func near(_ row: Language) -> Bool { row.identifier.hasPrefix(code + "-") }
150	            if let hit = list.first(where: { near($0) && $0.installed }) { return hit }
151	            if let hit = list.first(where: near) { return hit }
152	        }
153	        return list.first(where: { $0.installed }) ?? list.first
154	    }
155	
156	    /// The language a caller named — `en-US`, `en`, or a display name — or nil
157	    /// when nothing in `list` matches it.
158	    ///
159	    /// It is asked of BOTH lists, and that is the point: of
160	    /// `supportedLanguages()` to tell a misspelling from a real tag, and then
161	    /// of `languages()` to tell a real tag this Mac has a model for from one
162	    /// it has not. Those are the tool's two language refusals, and one
163	    /// matcher answers both so they cannot come to disagree about what
164	    /// counts as a match.
165	    static func language(matching name: String, in list: [Language]) -> Language? {
166	        let wanted = name.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)
167	        guard !wanted.isEmpty else { return nil }
168	        if let exact = list.first(where: {
169	            $0.identifier.caseInsensitiveCompare(wanted) == .orderedSame
170	        }) { return exact }
171	        if let named = list.first(where: {
172	            $0.displayName.caseInsensitiveCompare(wanted) == .orderedSame
173	        }) { return named }
174	        // `en` should find `en-US` — a caller who names a language rather
175	        // than a region means the one this Mac has.
176	        let prefix = wanted.replacingOccurrences(of: "_", with: "-").lowercased()
177	        return list.first { $0.identifier.lowercased().hasPrefix(prefix + "-") }
178	    }
179	}

3	// MARK: - Transcriber: extraction
4	
5	/// The extractor and what is made from it: a RANGE of any audio file written
6	/// to a mono 16 kHz 16-bit WAV (`extractAudio(url:name:range:to:cancel:)`),
7	/// the job form that names today's destination and calls it, the FLAC writer
8	/// C0's q2 chose for the upload, and `extractUpload`, which puts the two
9	/// together into the file a cloud run sends. `extractSettings` is the one
10	/// spelling of that format.
11	///
12	/// **The job form's behaviour is unchanged, and that is a claim.** The static
13	/// form is the block that was here verbatim, with the destination and the
14	/// range lifted out into its two arguments and `range.start` written where
15	/// the old code wrote the clip's `in`; the job form computes exactly the
16	/// destination and range the old code computed and calls it. The WAV a given
17	/// job extracts is byte-identical to the one the baseline tree's code wrote,
18	/// which is a row of `cloud_captions_probe.py` rather than a hope.
19	///
20	/// **The upload is a FLAC and the WAV is its fallback** (road map 6 §5a, §8).
21	/// C0's q2 measured a FLAC at 48.1% of the WAV's bytes whose decode is
22	/// sample-for-sample the same audio, with zero word-timing delta from the
23	/// service. It is written through `AVAudioFile`, NEVER `AVAssetWriter`:
24	/// `AVAssetWriter` has no `org.xiph.flac` file type on macOS 26 and refuses
25	/// it as an Objective-C exception, which Swift cannot catch (§3 q2). When the
26	/// FLAC write refuses for any other reason the WAV goes up instead and the
27	/// cache file records which was sent.
28	///
29	/// The on-device engine is untouched by all of it: it still hands the
30	/// recogniser the WAV of one clip's source window.
31	extension Transcriber {
32	
33	    // MARK: - Extraction
34	
35	    /// What the recogniser is handed: 16 kHz mono 16-bit LPCM in a `.wav`.
36	    ///
37	    /// Mono and 16 kHz because that is what speech recognition works in — a
38	    /// minute of it is under two megabytes, where the app's own 48 kHz stereo
39	    /// mix (`ExporterWriter.decodedAudioSettings`) would be eleven — and LPCM
40	    /// because an intermediate should cost no generation of its own. The
41	    /// stereo→mono downmix and the rate conversion are the reader's:
42	    /// `AVAssetReaderTrackOutput` does both, with no channel layout needed for
43	    /// one channel out.
44	    private static let extractSampleRate = 16000
45	
46	    private static let extractSettings: [String: Any] = [
47	        AVFormatIDKey: Int(kAudioFormatLinearPCM),
48	        AVSampleRateKey: extractSampleRate,
49	        AVNumberOfChannelsKey: 1,
50	        AVLinearPCMBitDepthKey: 16,
51	        AVLinearPCMIsFloatKey: false,
52	        AVLinearPCMIsBigEndianKey: false,
53	        AVLinearPCMIsNonInterleaved: false,
54	    ]
55	
56	    /// Writes the clip's source window to a temporary file and answers where
57	    /// it went and how long it really is.
58	    ///
59	    /// The length is counted in PCM frames rather than read back off the
60	    /// written asset: `AVAsset.duration` is deprecated in favour of an
61	    /// `async` accessor this file may not use (app/CLAUDE.md), and frames
62	    /// divided by a known sample rate is the more exact number anyway. It is
63	    /// what the engine's wait is bounded by, so it has to be the audio the
64	    /// engine was actually given, not the range that was asked for — a clip
65	    /// whose source window runs past the end of its file gets a shorter
66	    /// extract.
67	    ///
68	    /// The file goes in `NSTemporaryDirectory()`, never inside the package:
69	    /// it is an input to one recognition and is deleted the moment that
70	    /// recognition ends, unlike a reversed render, which is expensive enough
71	    /// to be worth carrying (`ReverseCache`'s doc argues the other side).
72	    ///
73	    /// Its whole body is the static form below, whose two arguments are the
74	    /// only things this adds: the destination and the range.
75	    func extractAudio(_ job: Job, cancel: CancelToken) throws -> (
76	        url: URL, seconds: Double
77	    ) {
78	        let destination = URL(fileURLWithPath: NSTemporaryDirectory())
79	            .appendingPathComponent("framejob-transcribe-\(UUID().uuidString).wav")
80	        let range = CMTimeRange(
81	            start: CompositionBuilder.time(job.sourceIn),
82	            duration: CompositionBuilder.time(max(1, job.sourceLength)))
83	        let frames = try Self.extractAudio(
84	            url: job.source, name: job.name, range: range, to: destination, cancel: cancel)
85	        return (destination, Double(frames) / Double(Self.extractSampleRate))
86	    }
87	
88	    /// A range of ANY audio file to a mono 16 kHz 16-bit WAV at `destination`,
89	    /// answering the PCM frames written.
90	    ///
91	    /// `range` is a SOURCE range. `Transcriber.wholeAsset` is the whole
92	    /// track, which is what the cloud engine uploads (R6-3: one upload per
93	    /// media, every clip derived from it); a clip's own window is what the
94	    /// on-device engine asks for.
95	    ///
96	    /// `progress` fires with the running frame count on the calling thread,
97	    /// never hopped, `run`'s convention.
98	    static func extractAudio(
99	        url: URL, name: String, range: CMTimeRange, to destination: URL, cancel: CancelToken,
100	        progress: ((Int) -> Void)? = nil
101	    ) throws -> Int {
102	        let asset = AVURLAsset(
103	            url: url, options: [AVURLAssetPreferPreciseDurationAndTimingKey: true])
104	        // The app's one synchronous track lookup, so the deprecation it costs
105	        // is paid once (`CompositionBuilder.firstTrack`'s doc).
106	        guard let track = CompositionBuilder.firstTrack(of: asset, mediaType: .audio) else {
107	            throw TranscribeError.unreadable(name)
108	        }
109	
110	        try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: destination)
111	
112	        let reader: AVAssetReader
113	        let writer: AVAssetWriter
114	        do {
115	            reader = try AVAssetReader(asset: asset)
116	            writer = try AVAssetWriter(outputURL: destination, fileType: .wav)
117	        } catch {
118	            throw TranscribeError.failed(error.localizedDescription)
119	        }
120	        // The MP3 encoder delay Core Audio leaves in (spec §11 SY-42): the read
121	        // and the session both start that far into the decode, so frame 0 of
122	        // the extract is the recording's `range.start`. Zero for every other
123	        // file, whose read is `range` as it always was.
124	        let trim = MP3Gapless.leadingTrim(of: url, track: track)
125	        let read = trim == .zero
126	            ? range : CMTimeRange(start: CMTimeAdd(range.start, trim), duration: range.duration)
127	        reader.timeRange = read
128	
129	        let output = AVAssetReaderTrackOutput(track: track, outputSettings: extractSettings)
130	        guard reader.canAdd(output) else { throw TranscribeError.unreadable(name) }
131	        reader.add(output)
132	        let input = AVAssetWriterInput(mediaType: .audio, outputSettings: extractSettings)
133	        input.expectsMediaDataInRealTime = false
134	        guard writer.canAdd(input) else { throw TranscribeError.unreadable(name) }
135	        writer.add(input)
136	
137	        guard reader.startReading() else {
138	            throw TranscribeError.failed(
139	                reader.error?.localizedDescription ?? "the audio could not be read")
140	        }
141	        guard writer.startWriting() else {
142	            throw TranscribeError.failed(
143	                writer.error?.localizedDescription ?? "the extract could not be opened")
144	        }
145	        // The session begins where the window does, so the first sample lands
146	        // at zero of the extract — which is what makes `project(_:in:)` a
147	        // single division with no `in` term in it.
148	        writer.startSession(atSourceTime: read.start)
149	
150	        var frames = 0
151	        while let sample = output.copyNextSampleBuffer() {
152	            if cancel.isCancelled {
153	                reader.cancelReading()
154	                writer.cancelWriting()
155	                try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: destination)
156	                throw TranscribeError.cancelled
157	            }
158	            // The wait leaves when the writer stops writing or Cancel lands
159	            // during it (#351), not only when the input is ready.
160	            if let failure = AudioRateCopy.append(
161	                sample, to: input, writer: writer, cancelled: { cancel.isCancelled },
162	                appendFailure: "the extract could not be written")
163	            {
164	                reader.cancelReading()
165	                writer.cancelWriting()
166	                try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: destination)
167	                if cancel.isCancelled { throw TranscribeError.cancelled }
168	                throw TranscribeError.failed(failure)
169	            }
170	            frames += CMSampleBufferGetNumSamples(sample)
171	            progress?(frames)
172	        }
173	        guard reader.status == .completed else {
174	            writer.cancelWriting()
175	            try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: destination)
176	            throw TranscribeError.failed(
177	                reader.error?.localizedDescription ?? "the audio stopped before it finished")
178	        }
179	        input.markAsFinished()
180	        // `finishWriting` closes the container on a queue of its own, and this
181	        // method's contract is that the file exists when it returns.
182	        let closed = DispatchSemaphore(value: 0)
183	        writer.finishWriting { closed.signal() }
184	        closed.wait()
185	        guard writer.status == .completed, frames > 0 else {
186	            try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: destination)
187	            throw TranscribeError.unreadable(name)
188	        }
189	        return frames
190	    }
191	
192	    // MARK: - What the cloud engine uploads
193	
194	    /// What was actually sent (road map 6 §5b's `uploaded_format`).
195	    enum UploadFormat: String {
196	        case flac
197	        case wav
198	    }
199	
200	    /// A file ready to upload, and everything the cache file needs to say
201	    /// about it.
202	    struct Upload: Equatable {
203	        let url: URL
204	        let format: UploadFormat
205	        /// PCM frames extracted, at `extractSampleRate`.
206	        let frames: Int
207	        /// `frames / 16000` — what was extracted, not what will be billed:
208	        /// `audio_duration` rounds UP (§3 q1).
209	        let seconds: Double
210	    }
211	
212	    /// The whole audio track. `.positiveInfinity` rather than a measured
213	    /// duration on purpose: `AVAsset.duration` and `AVAssetTrack.timeRange`
214	    /// are deprecated getters whose replacements are `async`, and
215	    /// `AVAssetReader` clamps a range that runs past the end of the asset, so
216	    /// the number is not needed at all.
217	    static let wholeAsset = CMTimeRange(start: .zero, duration: .positiveInfinity)
218	
219	    /// The WAV, decoded and re-encoded as a 16 kHz mono 16-bit FLAC.
220	    ///
221	    /// Streamed in 16 384-frame buffers, never the whole file in memory: the
222	    /// cloud engine's input is a media's WHOLE audio and ten hours of it is
223	    /// 1.1 GB of PCM. `cancel` is read per buffer, and `close()` — which
224	    /// `AVAudioFile` does on deinit — is forced before returning, because
225	    /// this function's contract is that the file is complete when it answers.
226	    ///
227	    /// The four settings are C0's, copied from
228	    /// `tools/proof/cloud_spike/extract.swift:167`, which is the run that
229	    /// measured the decode to be sample-for-sample the WAV's.
230	    static func writeFLAC(fromWAV wav: URL, to destination: URL, cancel: CancelToken) throws {
231	        try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: destination)
232	        guard
233	            let source = AVAudioFormat(
234	                commonFormat: .pcmFormatInt16, sampleRate: Double(extractSampleRate), channels: 1,
235	                interleaved: true)
236	        else { throw TranscribeError.failed("the extract format could not be described") }
237	        do {
238	            let reading = try AVAudioFile(forReading: wav, commonFormat: .pcmFormatInt16,
239	                                          interleaved: true)
240	            var file: AVAudioFile? = try AVAudioFile(
241	                forWriting: destination,
242	                settings: [
243	                    AVFormatIDKey: Int(kAudioFormatFLAC),
244	                    AVSampleRateKey: extractSampleRate,
245	                    AVNumberOfChannelsKey: 1,
246	                    AVLinearPCMBitDepthKey: 16,
247	                ], commonFormat: .pcmFormatInt16, interleaved: true)
248	            var left = reading.length
249	            while left > 0 {
250	                if cancel.isCancelled {
251	                    file = nil
252	                    try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: destination)
253	                    throw TranscribeError.cancelled
254	                }
255	                let count = AVAudioFrameCount(min(AVAudioFramePosition(flacBufferFrames), left))
256	                guard let buffer = AVAudioPCMBuffer(pcmFormat: source, frameCapacity: count)
257	                else { throw TranscribeError.failed("the FLAC buffer could not be made") }
258	                try reading.read(into: buffer, frameCount: count)
259	                guard buffer.frameLength > 0 else { break }
260	                try file?.write(from: buffer)
261	                left -= AVAudioFramePosition(buffer.frameLength)
262	            }
263	            // `AVAudioFile` has no `close()`; releasing it is the close, and
264	            // it is forced here rather than left to the end of the scope.
265	            file = nil
266	        } catch let error as TranscribeError {
267	            throw error
268	        } catch {
269	            throw TranscribeError.failed(error.localizedDescription)
270	        }
271	    }
272	
273	    /// 16 384 frames is about a second at 16 kHz — the spike's number.
274	    private static let flacBufferFrames = 16_384
275	
276	    /// A media's WHOLE audio as the file a cloud run uploads: the WAV first,
277	    /// then the FLAC beside it.
278	    ///
279	    /// **The fallback.** When `flac` throws anything but a cancellation the
280	    /// partial FLAC is removed and the WAV is answered as `.wav` — the upload
281	    /// is twice the bytes and the transcript is the same, which is a far
282	    /// better answer than refusing to transcribe because a codec was not
283	    /// there (§5a, §8). A cancellation is the person's instruction and
284	    /// propagates. On success the WAV goes, because it has done its job.
285	    ///
286	    /// `flac` is an argument so a probe can force the refusal and measure the
287	    /// fallback; its default IS `writeFLAC`, so the shipped path has one
288	    /// spelling.
289	    static func extractUpload(
290	        url: URL, name: String, cancel: CancelToken, progress: ((Int) -> Void)? = nil,
291	        flac: (URL, URL, CancelToken) throws -> Void = Transcriber.writeFLAC
292	    ) throws -> Upload {
293	        let stem = "framejob-upload-\(UUID().uuidString)"
294	        let wav = URL(fileURLWithPath: NSTemporaryDirectory())
295	            .appendingPathComponent("\(stem).wav")
296	        let frames = try extractAudio(
297	            url: url, name: name, range: wholeAsset, to: wav, cancel: cancel, progress: progress)
298	        let seconds = Double(frames) / Double(extractSampleRate)
299	        let compressed = URL(fileURLWithPath: NSTemporaryDirectory())
300	            .appendingPathComponent("\(stem).flac")
301	        do {
302	            try flac(wav, compressed, cancel)
303	        } catch TranscribeError.cancelled {
304	            try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: wav)
305	            try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: compressed)
306	            throw TranscribeError.cancelled
307	        } catch {
308	            try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: compressed)
309	            return Upload(url: wav, format: .wav, frames: frames, seconds: seconds)
310	        }
311	        try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: wav)
312	        return Upload(url: compressed, format: .flac, frames: frames, seconds: seconds)
313	    }
314	}

11	/// commits.** `style`, `replaceExisting`, `pagesRequest` and `looks` are the
12	/// four things `begin`, `beginCloud` and `finish` read, and they are computed
13	/// off the controls: the style off the popup's ITEM (app/CLAUDE.md's popup
14	/// rule), Replace only while the checkbox is live — which is the tool's two
15	/// rules read across (`AgentServer+Captions.swift`): a word style, and at
16	/// least one track `CaptionLayout.replaceableTracks` names — and each look
17	/// only while its box is enabled and on (spec §11 W-15).
18	///
19	/// **The preview is the renderer's own picture.** A sample page — the first
20	/// page `CaptionPages` makes of the scope's first clip's cached transcript,
21	/// else of `sampleText` — is laid out exactly as `place` would write it and
22	/// drawn by `LayerRenderers.textBitmap`, the routine the compositor uploads;
23	/// nothing is hand-drawn here but the plate and the scaling. A word style
24	/// shows two frames, the first and then the second word active — with a
25	/// ticked fill half done in both and a ticked pill half-way through its slide
26	/// in the second (`previewReveals`); the dim is not previewed. It is
27	/// redrawn only when its `PreviewKey` — the style, the first job's clip, the
28	/// canvas and the previewed looks — changes, so a keystroke in Vocabulary or
29	/// a click on Dim draws nothing.
30	///
31	/// **The style is remembered** under `CaptionStyle.defaultsKey`, read when
32	/// the popup is built and written when it changes, and never by the tool
33	/// (R6-2 read across). It is a display choice: not part of any transcript's
34	/// cache marker (R6-15), so a cached transcript stays a hit whatever is picked.
35	extension TranscribeSheetController {
36	
37	    /// What the preview was last drawn for; `refreshStyleRow` redraws on a change only.
38	    /// `looks` are the PREVIEWED ones: `dim` is always false there.
39	    struct PreviewKey: Equatable {
40	        let style: CaptionStyle
41	        let clip: UInt32?
42	        let canvas: CGSize
43	        var looks = CaptionLooks.none
44	    }
45	
46	    /// How far through its fill the preview draws the active word.
47	    static let previewFill = 0.5
48	    /// The slide's progress in the preview: `easeOut(0.2)` is 0.488, the pill
49	    /// drawn half-way between the first word and the second.
50	    static let previewGlide = 0.2
51	
52	    /// The preview's size in points: column 1 of the grid, 420 − 44 − 106 − 12.
53	    static let previewSize = CGSize(width: 258, height: 80)
54	
55	    /// Sentence case: each style's own `textCase` uppercases it through
56	    /// `laidContent` (`WordProps.swift`), so Subtitles and Karaoke preview as
57	    /// written and the other four in capitals — as `transcribe` commits them.
58	    static let sampleText = "This is how it looks"
59	
60	    /// The chosen style, read off the item; anything unreadable is Subtitles.
61	    var style: CaptionStyle {
62	        guard let raw = stylePopup.selectedItem?.representedObject as? String else {
63	            return .subtitles
64	        }
65	        return CaptionStyle(rawValue: raw) ?? .subtitles
66	    }
67	
68	    /// Replace only while the checkbox is live: a disabled box replaces
69	    /// nothing, whatever state it was left in.
70	    var replaceExisting: Bool {
71	        replaceCheckbox.isEnabled && replaceCheckbox.state == .on
72	    }
73	
74	    /// What each job's words are paged for: the style, on this canvas.
75	    var pagesRequest: CaptionPages.Request {
76	        CaptionPages.Request(
77	            style: style,
78	            canvas: CGSize(width: snapshot.canvas.width, height: snapshot.canvas.height))
79	    }
80	
81	    // MARK: - The three rows
82	
83	    /// Grid row 7: Subtitles, then the five word styles, in
84	    /// `CaptionStyle.allCases` order, opening on the remembered one.
85	    func makeStyleRow() -> [NSView] {
86	        stylePopup.removeAllItems()
87	        stylePopup.menu?.autoenablesItems = false
88	        for style in CaptionStyle.allCases {
89	            let item = NSMenuItem(title: style.displayName, action: nil, keyEquivalent: "")
90	            item.representedObject = style.rawValue
91	            stylePopup.menu?.addItem(item)
92	        }
93	        let remembered = defaults.string(forKey: CaptionStyle.defaultsKey)
94	        let wanted = CaptionStyle.allCases.first { $0.rawValue == remembered } ?? .subtitles
95	        if let index = stylePopup.itemArray.firstIndex(where: {
96	            $0.representedObject as? String == wanted.rawValue
97	        }) {
98	            stylePopup.selectItem(at: index)
99	        }
100	        stylePopup.font = DS.sans(13)
101	        stylePopup.target = self
102	        stylePopup.action = #selector(styleChanged(_:))
103	        stylePopup.widthAnchor.constraint(equalToConstant: 200).isActive = true
104	        return [fieldLabel("Style:"), stylePopup]
105	    }
106	
107	    /// Grid row 9: the preview, the full width of the controls column.
108	    func makePreviewRow() -> [NSView] {
109	        previewView.imageScaling = .scaleNone
110	        previewView.imageFrameStyle = .none
111	        previewView.widthAnchor.constraint(equalToConstant: Self.previewSize.width)
112	            .isActive = true
113	        previewView.heightAnchor.constraint(equalToConstant: Self.previewSize.height)
114	            .isActive = true
115	        return [fieldLabel(""), previewView]
116	    }
117	
118	    /// Grid row 10: the checkbox, and under it the tracks it will replace.
119	    func makeReplaceRow() -> [NSView] {
120	        replaceCheckbox.font = DS.sans(12)
121	        replaceCheckbox.target = self
122	        replaceCheckbox.action = #selector(controlChanged(_:))
123	        replaceLabel.font = DS.sans(11)
124	        replaceLabel.textColor = DS.textMuted
125	        replaceLabel.isEditable = false
126	        replaceLabel.preferredMaxLayoutWidth = Self.previewSize.width
127	        let stack = NSStackView(views: [replaceCheckbox, replaceLabel])
128	        stack.orientation = .vertical
129	        stack.alignment = .leading
130	        stack.spacing = 4
131	        return [fieldLabel("Replace:"), stack]
132	    }
133	
134	    /// The Style popup: remember the choice, and recompute.
135	    @objc func styleChanged(_ sender: Any?) {
136	        defaults.set(style.rawValue, forKey: CaptionStyle.defaultsKey)
137	        refresh()
138	    }
139	
140	    /// The four rows' state, recomputed — `refresh()` calls it on the way
141	    /// out, whichever engine it dispatched to. The looks row first: the
142	    /// preview's key reads `looks`, which reads each box's `isEnabled`.
143	    func refreshStyleRow() {
144	        refreshLooksRow()
145	        let jobs = jobs(in: scope)
146	        let replaceable = CaptionLayout.replaceableTracks(in: snapshot, jobs: jobs)
147	        let live = style.isWordStyle && !replaceable.isEmpty
148	        replaceCheckbox.isEnabled = live
149	        if !live { replaceCheckbox.state = .off }
150	        replaceLabel.isHidden = !live
151	        replaceLabel.stringValue = live ? replaceText(replaceable) : ""
152	        var previewed = looks
153	        previewed.dim = false
154	        let key = PreviewKey(
155	            style: style, clip: jobs.first?.clip,
156	            canvas: CGSize(width: snapshot.canvas.width, height: snapshot.canvas.height),
157	            looks: previewed)
158	        if key != previewKey {
159	            previewKey = key
160	            previewView.image = preview()
161	        }
162	    }
163	
164	    /// "Replaces “Captions” (12 captions), “Captions 2” (3 captions)." — the
165	    /// tracks by name, in stack order, each with its clip count.
166	    private func replaceText(_ tracks: [UInt32]) -> String {
167	        let named = tracks.map { id -> String in
168	            let name = snapshot.tracks.first { $0.id == id }?.name ?? "track \(id)"
169	            let count = snapshot.clips.filter { $0.track == id }.count
170	            return "“\(name)” (\(count) caption\(count == 1 ? "" : "s"))"
171	        }
172	        return "Replaces " + named.joined(separator: ", ") + "."
173	    }
174	
175	    // MARK: - The preview
176	
177	    /// `sampleText`'s five tokens, one every 0.3 s from 0, each 0.18 s long.
178	    static var fixedSampleWords: [CaptionCues.Word] {
179	        sampleText.split(separator: " ").enumerated().map { index, token in
180	            let start = Ticks(index) * 180_000
181	            return CaptionCues.Word(text: String(token), start: start, end: start + 108_000)
182	        }
183	    }
184	
185	    /// The words the preview pages: the first job's own words, up to twelve,
186	    /// when a cached transcript already has them, else `fixedSampleWords`.
187	    /// The ANSWER is cached per clip, a miss included — `refresh` runs per
188	    /// keystroke, and `MediaTranscript.read` is a disk read hit or miss.
189	    func sampleWords() -> [CaptionCues.Word] {
190	        guard let job = jobs(in: scope).first else { return Self.fixedSampleWords }
191	        if let cached = sampleWordsCache[job.clip] { return cached }
192	        var words: [CaptionCues.Word] = []
193	        if let directory = document?.cacheDirectory,
194	            let file = MediaTranscript.read(for: job.media, in: directory)
195	        {
196	            words = Array(MediaTranscript.captionWords(for: job, in: file).prefix(12))
197	        }
198	        let answer = words.isEmpty ? Self.fixedSampleWords : words
199	        sampleWordsCache[job.clip] = answer
200	        return answer
201	    }
202	
203	    /// The page's text props as `CaptionLayout.place` writes them: a word
204	    /// style's are `CaptionStyle.textProps` at the page's own size and width —
205	    /// the one construction the pager measured and `pagePatch` commits, with
206	    /// the sheet's `looks` as `place` is handed them — and Subtitles' are the
207	    /// Caption preset with its wrap box, mirrored.
208	    func previewProps(for cue: CaptionLayout.Cue, canvas: CGSize) -> TextProps {
209	        guard style.isWordStyle else {
210	            let preset = CaptionLayout.captionPreset
211	            return TextProps(
212	                content: cue.text, font: preset.font,
213	                size: preset.size(on: canvas),
214	                align: preset.align, valign: "middle", backdrop: preset.backdrop,
215	                width: Double(canvas.width) * CaptionLayout.wrapFraction)
216	        }
217	        return style.textProps(
218	            content: cue.text, size: cue.size ?? style.size(for: canvas), width: cue.width,
219	            looks: looks)
220	    }
221	
222	    /// A word style's two preview frames: the first word active, then the
223	    /// second (the first again on a one-word page), each with the fill at
224	    /// `previewFill` when Fill is on, and the second with the pill at
225	    /// `previewGlide` when Slide is on and there is a word to slide from.
226	    static func previewReveals(tokens: Int, looks: CaptionLooks) -> [RecipeReveal] {
227	        let fill = looks.fill ? previewFill : nil
228	        let glide = looks.slide && tokens >= 2 ? previewGlide : nil
229	        return [
230	            RecipeReveal(word: 1, wordPop: 1, wordFill: fill),
231	            RecipeReveal(word: min(2, tokens), wordPop: 1, wordGlide: glide, wordFill: fill),
232	        ]
233	    }
234	
235	    /// The sample page drawn by the renderer: two frames for a word style
236	    /// (`previewReveals`), one for Subtitles, each
237	    /// scaled to fit a 258×36 slot, stacked 8 pt apart over the plate, at 2×.
238	    func preview() -> NSImage? {
239	        let canvas = CGSize(width: snapshot.canvas.width, height: snapshot.canvas.height)
240	        let frame = max(snapshot.canvas.fps.frameDuration, 1)
241	        guard
242	            let cue = CaptionPages.samplePage(
243	                sampleWords(), request: pagesRequest, frame: frame)
244	        else { return nil }
245	        let props = previewProps(for: cue, canvas: canvas)
246	        let reveals =
247	            style.isWordStyle
248	            ? Self.previewReveals(tokens: props.tokenCount, looks: looks)
249	            : [RecipeReveal.whole]
250	        let size = Self.previewSize
251	        let scale: CGFloat = 2
252	        guard
253	            let context = LayerRenderers.bitmap(
254	                CGSize(width: size.width * scale, height: size.height * scale))
255	        else { return nil }
256	        context.setFillColor(DS.captionPreviewPlate.cgColor)
257	        context.fill(CGRect(x: 0, y: 0, width: context.width, height: context.height))
258	        context.scaleBy(x: scale, y: scale)
259	        context.interpolationQuality = .high
260	
261	        let slot = CGSize(width: size.width, height: 36)
262	        let gap: CGFloat = 8
263	        let count = CGFloat(reveals.count)
264	        // From the TOP, in points; the context is y-up.
265	        var top = (size.height - count * slot.height - (count - 1) * gap) / 2
266	        for reveal in reveals {
267	            if let bitmap = LayerRenderers.textBitmap(props, reveal: reveal),
268	                let image = bitmap.makeImage()
269	            {
270	                let fit = min(
271	                    slot.width / CGFloat(image.width), slot.height / CGFloat(image.height))
272	                let drawn = CGSize(
273	                    width: CGFloat(image.width) * fit, height: CGFloat(image.height) * fit)
274	                context.draw(
275	                    image,
276	                    in: CGRect(
277	                        x: (size.width - drawn.width) / 2,
278	                        y: size.height - top - slot.height + (slot.height - drawn.height) / 2,
279	                        width: drawn.width, height: drawn.height))
280	            }
281	            top += slot.height + gap
282	        }
283	        guard let image = context.makeImage() else { return nil }
284	        return NSImage(cgImage: image, size: size)
285	    }
286	}

132-                    + "track of its own — File ▸ Generate Captions…. They are ordinary text "
133-                    + "clips in the Caption preset, exactly what import_captions makes, so they "
134-                    + "render in the preview, in render_frame and in an export (burn-in) and "
135-                    + "can be retimed with move_clip or restyled with set_text. Cues are at "
136-                    + "most two lines of 42 characters and at most 6 s, with a frame between "
137-                    + "them. A word caption STYLE (every style but subtitles) makes PAGES "
138-                    + "instead: each page is filled to the width it will MEASURE on this "
139-                    + "canvas in that style — at most 0.86 of the canvas width — not to a word "
140-                    + "count, on one line (karaoke: up to two); a page also closes at a "
141-                    + "change of speaker, a gap of 0.25 s or more, a word ending . ? ! or …, "
142-                    + "3 s on screen, and one_word's single word; a lone word too wide "
143-                    + "shrinks to 80% before it wraps. Pages stay within their own clip and "
144-                    + "abut the next page where the gap is under 0.25 s, else hold 0.5 s "
145-                    + "after the last word. Each placed page is a text clip in the style's "
146-                    + "face, case and word_style carrying its words' timings, so the word "
147-                    + "being said is drawn as the style says. The result carries the cues "
148-                    + "themselves in TICKS whether or not they were placed — with a word "
149-                    + "style each cue adds words, [{start, end, text}] in timeline ticks, and "
150-                    + "size where a lone word shrank — names the engine that ran, reports "
151-                    + "under skipped every clip you named that cannot be transcribed, and, "
152-                    + "whenever replace was given, lists under replaced the tracks it "
153-                    + "removed. slide, fill and dim each add a look to a word style's pages; "
154-                    + "whenever one of the three was given, a placed run lists under looks "
155-                    + "the ones that were on. "
156-                    + "ENGINE \"apple\" (the default) is ON-DEVICE speech recognition and "
157-                    + "nothing leaves this Mac. It needs no grant and has no length ceiling. "
158-                    + "Its models are installed per Mac: a language whose model is not "
159-                    + "installed is refused by name and nothing is changed — this tool never "
160-                    + "downloads one; a person installs it from File ▸ Generate Captions…'s "
161-                    + "Download row. "
162-                    + "ENGINE \"assemblyai\" sends the audio of every media file behind the "
163-                    + "clips you named — the WHOLE file, not just the parts in use — to "
164-                    + "AssemblyAI, a cloud service that transcribes it and is billed for it, "
165-                    + "and the transcript is deleted from AssemblyAI once the words have been "
166-                    + "read back; do not choose it for somebody else's recording without their "
167-                    + "say-so. New transcription needs an API key; a nonempty batch whose every "
168-                    + "media has a current packaged transcript can be reused without a key "
169-                    + "or network request, unless refresh is true. Pending remote deletion "
